The sage of science, Einstein, was sitting in a depressive and pensive mood one evening. His eyes were brimming with tears. The pain was evident on his face. He peeped out of the window of his room. The sun had set a few minutes back. The sky was filled with a reddish glow. At this sunset, he felt that it was humanity that had sunk into devilish darkness and the reddish glow in the sky was the blood of humanity spilling all over the sky from earth. With tired steps, he walked back to his chair and settled down. It was the 9th of August 1945. Three days back, he had felt the same agony as if someone had torn him apart. He was deeply hurt and depressed when he heard on the radio that America had dropped an atom bomb on the Japanese city, Hiroshima. Today, within three days another bomb was dropped on another city, Nagasaki and lakhs of people had been killed.

He had heard that the blast released so much energy that it had paled all past destructions in comparison and death had played out a pitiable dance of destruction. The flames that broke out of the bomb were burning, melting, and exploding buildings. Scared of the heat of the bomb, people had jumped into lakes and rivers, but the water was boiling and the people too were burnt and killed. The animals in the water were already boiled to death. Animals, trees, herbs, fragrant flowering plants were all turned into ashes. The atomic energy destruction had just not stopped there. It had entered the atmosphere there and had spread radiation that would affect people for generations to come and would also bring about destructive irreversible biological change in animals and plants.

As the news of the atomic attack reached Einstein, and he became aware of the glaring horror of the abuse of atomic energy, his distress and restlessness knew no bounds. He could not control himself and picked up his violin to turn his mind on to other things. While playing the violin, he tried to dissolve his distress in its sad notes, but couldn’t. He was burning on the embers of destruction; his heart was filled with an ocean of agony and tears just continued streaming uncontrollably out of his eyes. Night had fallen. His daughter came up and asked him to eat something as he had not taken anything for the last four days. His voice was restrained and he said, “I don’t feel like eating.”

He could not sleep that night. Lying down, he was thinking how he had drawn the attention of the then American President Roosevelt towards the destructive powers of an atomic bomb. He had thought that this would be used to scare Hitler and put an end to the barbarism that Hitler was up to. However, Roosevelt kept him in the dark and made false promises. Eventually, he had abused Einstein’s equation of E = mc2 that resulted in the destructive experiments. His actions had made science and scientists as murderers. Einstein kept on thinking for a long time. Eventually, he slipped into sleep. When he woke up at dawn, there was a new dawn in him too. The atomic threat had transformed his heart.

Why did Einstein refuse to eat?

Paragraph 2 of the passage: “He refused to eat, feeling guilty that he had not done enough to help those suffering from the war and its aftermath.”

So, option (a) is the correct answer.

Paragraph 2 of the passage: “He refused to eat, feeling guilty that he had not done enough to help those suffering from the war and its aftermath.”

So, option a is the correct answer.

At this sunset, he felt that it was humanity that had sunk into devilish darkness and the reddish glow in the sky was the blood of humanity spilling all over the sky from earth. With tired steps, he walked back to his chair and settled down. It was the 9th of August 1945. Three days back, he had felt the same agony as if someone had torn him apart. He was deeply hurt and depressed when he heard on the radio that America had dropped an atom bomb on the Japanese city, Hiroshima. Today, within three days another bomb was dropped on another city, Nagasaki and lakhs of people had been killed.

He had heard that the blast released so much energy that it had paled all past destructions in comparison and death had played out a pitiable dance of destruction. The flames that broke out of the bomb were burning, melting, and exploding buildings. Scared of the heat of the bomb, people had jumped into lakes and rivers, but the water was boiling and the people too were burnt and killed. The animals in the water were already boiled to death. Animals, trees, herbs, fragrant flowering plants were all turned into ashes. The atomic energy destruction had just not stopped there. It had entered the atmosphere there and had spread radiation that would affect people for generations to come and would also bring about destructive irreversible biological change in animals and plants.

As the news of the atomic attack reached Einstein, and he became aware of the glaring horror of the abuse of atomic energy, his distress and restlessness knew no bounds. He could not control himself and picked up his violin to turn his mind on to other things. While playing the violin, he tried to dissolve his distress in its sad notes, but couldn’t. He was burning on the embers of destruction; his heart was filled with an ocean of agony and tears just continued streaming uncontrollably out of his eyes. Night had fallen. His daughter came up and asked him to eat something as he had not taken anything for the last four days. His voice was restrained and he said, “I don’t feel like eating.”

He could not sleep that night. Lying down, he was thinking how he had drawn the attention of the then American President Roosevelt towards the destructive powers of an atomic bomb. He had thought that this would be used to scare Hitler and put an end to the barbarism that Hitler was up to. However, Roosevelt kept him in the dark and made false promises. Eventually, he had abused Einstein’s equation of E = mc2 that resulted in the destructive experiments. His actions had made science and scientists as murderers. Einstein kept on thinking for a long time. Eventually, he slipped into sleep. When he woke up at dawn, there was a new dawn in him too. The atomic threat had transformed his heart.

Read the following passage and answer the questions given after it.

Wetlands are amongst the most productive ecosystems on the Earth and provide many important services to human society. They exhibit enormous diversity according to their genesis, geographical location, water regime and chemistry, dominant species, and soil and sediment characteristics. Globally, the areal extent of wetland ecosystems ranges from 917 million hectares (m ha) to more than 1275 m ha. One of the ﬁrst widely used wetland classiﬁcations systems, devised by Cowardin et al., 1979, categorized wetlands into marine (coastal wetlands), estuarine (including deltas, tidal marshes, and mangrove swamps), lacustrine (lakes), riverine (along rivers and streams), and palustrine ( marshes, swamps and bogs) based on their hydrological, ecological and geological characteristics.

Ramsar Convention on Wetlands was an international treaty signed in 1971. Overall, 1052 sites in Europe; 289 sites in Asia; 359 sites in Africa; 175 sites in South America; 211 sites in North America; and 79 sites in Oceania region have been identiﬁed as Ramsar sites or wetlands of International importance.

As per the Ramsar Convention deﬁnition most of the natural water bodies (such as rivers, lakes, coastal lagoons, mangroves, peat land, coral reefs) and man- made wetlands (such as ponds, farm ponds, irrigated ﬁelds, sacred groves, salt pans, reservoirs, gravel pits, sewage farms and canals) in India constitute the wetland ecosystem distributed in different geographical regions ranging from Himalayas to Deccan plateau. As of February, 2022, India has 49 Ramsar sites covering an area of 10,93,636 hectares, the highest in South Asia.

As per the estimates, India has about 757.06 thousand wetlands with a total wetland area of 15.3 m ha, accounting for nearly 4.7% of the total geographical area of the country . Out of this, areas under inland wetlands accounts for 69%, coastal wetlands 27%, and other wetlands (smaller than 2.25 ha) 4%.

Gujarat has the highest proportion (17.5%) and Mizoram has the lowest proportion (0.66%) of the area under wetlands. Among Union Territories, Lakshadweep has the highest proportion (around 96%) and Chandigarh has the least proportion (3%) of geographical area under wetlands.

Match the continents with the number of Ramsar sites.

Read the following passage and answer the questions given after it.

Wetlands are amongst the most productive ecosystems on the Earth and provide many important services to human society. They exhibit enormous diversity according to their genesis, geographical location, water regime and chemistry, dominant species, and soil and sediment characteristics. Globally, the areal extent of wetland ecosystems ranges from 917 million hectares (m ha) to more than 1275 m ha. One of the ﬁrst widely used wetland classiﬁcations systems, devised by Cowardin et al., 1979, categorized wetlands into marine (coastal wetlands), estuarine (including deltas, tidal marshes, and mangrove swamps), lacustrine (lakes), riverine (along rivers and streams), and palustrine ( marshes, swamps and bogs) based on their hydrological, ecological and geological characteristics.

Ramsar Convention on Wetlands was an international treaty signed in 1971. Overall, 1052 sites in Europe; 289 sites in Asia; 359 sites in Africa; 175 sites in South America; 211 sites in North America; and 79 sites in Oceania region have been identiﬁed as Ramsar sites or wetlands of International importance.

As per the Ramsar Convention deﬁnition most of the natural water bodies (such as rivers, lakes, coastal lagoons, mangroves, peat land, coral reefs) and man- made wetlands (such as ponds, farm ponds, irrigated ﬁelds, sacred groves, salt pans, reservoirs, gravel pits, sewage farms and canals) in India constitute the wetland ecosystem distributed in different geographical regions ranging from Himalayas to Deccan plateau. As of February, 2022, India has 49 Ramsar sites covering an area of 10,93,636 hectares, the highest in South Asia.

As per the estimates, India has about 757.06 thousand wetlands with a total wetland area of 15.3 m ha, accounting for nearly 4.7% of the total geographical area of the country . Out of this, areas under inland wetlands accounts for 69%, coastal wetlands 27%, and other wetlands (smaller than 2.25 ha) 4%.

Gujarat has the highest proportion (17.5%) and Mizoram has the lowest proportion (0.66%) of the area under wetlands. Among Union Territories, Lakshadweep has the highest proportion (around 96%) and Chandigarh has the least proportion (3%) of geographical area under wetlands.

Under which category of wetlands, are delta and mangrove swamps included?
expl:
it is mentioned in the passage, “1979 classification system categorizes wetlands into five types, which includes estuarine wetlands comprising of deltas, tidal marshes, and mangrove swamps.”

So, option (d) is correct.

it is mentioned in the passage, “1979 classification system categorizes wetlands into five types, which includes estuarine wetlands comprising of deltas, tidal marshes, and mangrove swamps.”

So, option d is correct.

Read the following passage and answer the questions given after it.

Notwithstanding logistical challenges posed by COVID19 pandemic, India continues to expand its rice exports footprint in the African, Asian and European Union markets, thus having the largest share in global rice trade. The robust global demand also helped India’s growth in rice exports.

In 2020-21, India’s rice exports (Basmati and Non-Basmati) rose by a huge 87 per cent to 17.72 Million Tonne (MT) from 9.49 MT achieved in 2019-20.

In terms of value realisation, India’s rice exports rose by 38 per cent to USD 8815 million in 2020-21 from USD 6397 million reported in 2019-20. In terms of Rupees, India’s rice export grew by 44 per cent to Rs 65298 crore in 2020-21 from Rs 45379 crore in the previous year.

In the first seven months of the current financial year (2021-22), India’s rice exports rose by more than 33 per cent to 11.79 MT from 8.91 MT achieved during April-October, 2020-21. It is anticipated that India’s rice exports in 2021-22 would likely surpass the record feet of 17.72 MT achieved in 2020-21.

In 2020-21, India shipped non-basmati rice to nine countries - Timor-Leste, Puerto Rico, Brazil, Papua New Guinea, Zimbabwe, Burundi, Eswatini, Myanmar and Nicaragua, where exports were carried out for the first time or earlier the shipment was smaller in volume.

India’s Non-Basmati rice exports was valued at USD 4796 million (Rs 35448crore) in 2020- 21, with Basmati Rice exports a close second at USD 4018 million (Rs 29,849 crore).

In terms of volume of Basmati rice exports in 2020-21, top ten countries – Saudi Arabia, Iran, Iraq, Yemen, United Arab Emirates, United States of America, Kuwait, United Kingdom, Qatar and Oman have a share of close to 80 per cent in total shipments of aromatic long grained rice from India.

Top ten countries – Nepal, Benin, Bangladesh, Senegal, Togo, Cote D Ivoire, Guinea, Malaysia, Iraq, United Arab Emirates – have a share of 57 per cent in India’s total exports of non-Basmati rice in 2020-21 in terms of volume.

What is the estimate of rice export in the year 2021-22?
opts: It will remain the same as the 17.72 MT rice export achieved in 2020-21.
It will not pass beyond the 17.72 MT rice export achieved in 2020-21.
It may fall below the 17.72 MT rice export achieved in 2020-21.
It will exceed the 17.72 MT rice export achieved in 2020-21.
expl:
The last line of the third paragraph says;

It is anticipated that India’s rice exports in 2021-22 would likely surpass the record feet of 17.72 MT achieved in 2020-21.
raw_sol:
The last line of the third paragraph says;

It is anticipated that India’s rice exports in 2021-22 would likely surpass the record feet of 17.72 MT achieved in 2020-21.

qhtml:
Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

As the Sun inches closer to its peak activity in its solar cycle, an explosion has been picked up behind the north-eastern limb of the star in our solar system. Solar observatories saw bits and pieces of the explosion, which remain obscured in view from Earth's orbit.

The explosion was spotted on 31 July at around 2309 UT and Earth-orbiting satellites registered a long-lasting C9.3-class solar flare. "The intensity is probably an underestimate because it was partially eclipsed by the edge of the sun. Nasa's Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO) saw hot debris flying away from the blast site," space weather, which tracks the solar activity, reported.

While the explosion was powerful, experts have predicted that Earth is not in the line of fire from the Sun. Scientists are expected to get a view of the active region later this week as it comes to sight. Earth is not in the line of fire. The explosion is significant because it may herald an active region set to emerge over the sun's north-eastern limb later this week. A new sunspot group could bring an end to weeks of relative quiet," space weather said in its report.

Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word from the passage.

Peak
expl:
Peak – the highest point of something.

Zenith – the culmination or highest point of something.

Glance – to take a quick look or glimpse at something.

Point – a specific location or a sharp end of something.

Bottom – the base of something.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.
raw_sol:
Peak – the highest point of something.

Zenith – the culmination or highest point of something.

Glance – to take a quick look or glimpse at something.

Point – a specific location or a sharp end of something.

Bottom – the base of something.

Hence, option b is the correct answer.

qhtml:
Read the following passage and answer the questions given after it.

Tens of thousands of people who lost their homes in a catastrophic earthquake huddled around campfires in the bitter cold and clamoured for food and water on Thursday, three days after the temblor hit Turkey and Syria and killed more than 19,300 on Monday, 6th February, 2023.

Emergency crews used pick axes, shovels and jackhammers to dig through twisted metal and concrete - and occasionally still pulled out survivors.

In the Turkish city of Antakya, dozens scrambled for aid in front of a truck distributing children's coats and other supplies. Many of those who lost their homes found shelter in tents, stadiums and other temporary accommodation, but others slept outdoors.

In Antakya, over 100 bodies were awaiting identification in a makeshift morgue outside a hospital.

Authorities called off search-and-rescue operations in the cities of Kilis and Sanliurfa, where destruction was not as severe as in other impacted regions.

The U.N. is authorised to deliver aid through only one border crossing, and road damage has prevented that thus far. U.N. Officials pleaded for humanitarian concerns to take precedence over wartime politics.

The scale of loss and suffering remained massive. Turkish authorities said on Thursday that the death toll had risen to more than 16,100 in the country, with more than 64,000 injured.

In Syria, which includes government-held and rebel-held areas, more than 3,100 have been reported dead and more than 5,000 injured.

Rescue teams urged quiet in the hope of hearing stifled pleas for help, and the Syrian paramedic group known as the White Helmets noted that every second could mean saving a life. But more and more often, the teams pulled out dead bodies.

It was not clear how many people were still unaccounted for in both countries.

Turkey's disaster-management agency said more than 110,000 rescue personnel were now taking part in the effort and more than 5,500 vehicles, including tractors, cranes, bulldozers and excavators had been shipped.

The Foreign Ministry said 95 countries have offered help. More than half of that number have sent a total of nearly 6,500 rescuers. Another 2,400 more are still expected to arrive.

International aid for Syria was far more sparse.

Efforts there have been hampered by the civil war and the isolation of the rebel-held region along the border that is surrounded by Russia-backed government forces.

The passage highlights all the following except
opts: the foreign aid being offered to Turkey and Syria
the rescue work being carried out in Turkey and Syria
Syria’s rebel-held areas and the Civil war going on there
the suffering of people in the earthquake hit areas of Turkey and Syria
expl:
The passage does not highlight the rebel-held areas and the civil war going on there.

It highlights the earthquake that hit both Turkey and Syria, the suffering of the affected people and the rescue work being carried out there.
raw_sol:
The passage does not highlight the rebel-held areas and the civil war going on there.

It highlights the earthquake that hit both Turkey and Syria, the suffering of the affected people and the rescue work being carried out there.

Tens of thousands of people who lost their homes in a catastrophic earthquake huddled around campfires in the bitter cold and clamoured for food and water on Thursday, three days after the temblor hit Turkey and Syria and killed more than 19,300 on Monday, 6th February, 2023.

Emergency crews used pick axes, shovels and jackhammers to dig through twisted metal and concrete - and occasionally still pulled out survivors.

In the Turkish city of Antakya, dozens scrambled for aid in front of a truck distributing children's coats and other supplies. Many of those who lost their homes found shelter in tents, stadiums and other temporary accommodation, but others slept outdoors.

In Antakya, over 100 bodies were awaiting identification in a makeshift morgue outside a hospital.

Authorities called off search-and-rescue operations in the cities of Kilis and Sanliurfa, where destruction was not as severe as in other impacted regions.

The U.N. is authorised to deliver aid through only one border crossing, and road damage has prevented that thus far. U.N. Officials pleaded for humanitarian concerns to take precedence over wartime politics.

In Syria, which includes government-held and rebel-held areas, more than 3,100 have been reported dead and more than 5,000 injured.

Rescue teams urged quiet in the hope of hearing stifled pleas for help, and the Syrian paramedic group known as the White Helmets noted that every second could mean saving a life. But more and more often, the teams pulled out dead bodies.

Notwithstanding logistical challenges posed by COVID19 pandemic, India continues to expand its rice exports footprint in the African, Asian and European Union markets, thus having the largest share in global rice trade. The robust global demand also helped India’s growth in rice exports.

In 2020-21, India’s rice exports (Basmati and Non-Basmati) rose by a huge 87 per cent to 17.72 Million Tonne (MT) from 9.49 MT achieved in 2019-20.

In terms of value realisation, India’s rice exports rose by 38 per cent to USD 8815 million in 2020-21 from USD 6397 million reported in 2019-20. In terms of Rupees, India’s rice export grew by 44 per cent to Rs 65298 crore in 2020-21 from Rs 45379 crore in the previous year.

In the first seven months of the current financial year (2021-22), India’s rice exports rose by more than 33 per cent to 11.79 MT from 8.91 MT achieved during April-October, 2020-21. It is anticipated that India’s rice exports in 2021-22 would likely surpass the record feet of 17.72 MT achieved in 2020-21.

In 2020-21, India shipped non-basmati rice to nine countries - Timor-Leste, Puerto Rico, Brazil, Papua New Guinea, Zimbabwe, Burundi, Eswatini, Myanmar and Nicaragua, where exports were carried out for the first time or earlier the shipment was smaller in volume.

India’s Non-Basmati rice exports was valued at USD 4796 million (Rs 35448crore) in 2020- 21, with Basmati Rice exports a close second at USD 4018 million (Rs 29,849 crore).

In terms of volume of Basmati rice exports in 2020-21, top ten countries – Saudi Arabia, Iran, Iraq, Yemen, United Arab Emirates, United States of America, Kuwait, United Kingdom, Qatar and Oman have a share of close to 80 per cent in total shipments of aromatic long grained rice from India.

Top ten countries – Nepal, Benin, Bangladesh, Senegal, Togo, Cote D Ivoire, Guinea, Malaysia, Iraq, United Arab Emirates – have a share of 57 per cent in India’s total exports of non-Basmati rice in 2020-21 in terms of volume.

Chlorophyll

Subhas Chandra Bose, a prominent Indian nationalist leader, was convinced that India could not achieve independence without the use of force, and he believed that a military campaign was necessary to achieve this goal. In 1942, Bose formed the Indian National Army (INA) with the help of the Japanese.
Bose travelled to Japan in 1941 to seek their support in the struggle against British rule in India. The Japanese were interested in having Bose’s help in their own efforts to expand their influence in Southeast Asia. Bose’s vision was to create a military force to fight against the British in India with the help of Japanese weapons and training. The INA was formed in Singapore in September 1942 with the slogan ‘Jai Hind’ (Victory to India). The INA consisted of soldiers who were primarily from the Indian community in Southeast Asia. They were trained by Japanese officers and were equipped with Japanese weapons. The INA fought alongside Japanese forces in Burma and other parts of Southeast Asia during World War II. Bose’s leadership of the INA and his military campaigns against the British in India made him a popular figure among many Indians. The consequences of the formation of the INA were significant. The INA’s campaigns against the British in India and the Indian soldiers’ role in the Burma campaign had a psychological impact on the British forces. The British were shocked that Indian soldiers had turned against them, undermining their confidence in maintaining control over India. The INA also had a significant impact on the Indian independence movement. Bose’s vision of a socialist India with equal rights for all citizens inspired many Indians. The INA became a symbol of the struggle against British colonialism, and Bose’s slogan of ‘Jai Hind’ became a rallying cry for the independence movement.
However, the INA’s military campaigns were not successful in achieving their goal of freeing India from British rule. The INA suffered significant losses in battles, and their efforts were undermined by the Japanese surrender in 1945.
What was the significance of Bose’s slogan ‘Jai Hind’?

It symbolised the struggle against British colonialism.

Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.
Subhas Chandra Bose, a prominent Indian nationalist leader, was convinced that India could not achieve independence without the use of force, and he believed that a military campaign was necessary to achieve this goal. In 1942, Bose formed the Indian National Army (INA) with the help of the Japanese.
Bose travelled to Japan in 1941 to seek their support in the struggle against British rule in India. The Japanese were interested in having Bose’s help in their own efforts to expand their influence in Southeast Asia. Bose’s vision was to create a military force to fight against the British in India with the help of Japanese weapons and training. The INA was formed in Singapore in September 1942 with the slogan ‘Jai Hind’ (Victory to India). The INA consisted of soldiers who were primarily from the Indian community in Southeast Asia. They were trained by Japanese officers and were equipped with Japanese weapons. The INA fought alongside Japanese forces in Burma and other parts of Southeast Asia during World War II. Bose’s leadership of the INA and his military campaigns against the British in India made him a popular figure among many Indians. The consequences of the formation of the INA were significant. The INA’s campaigns against the British in India and the Indian soldiers’ role in the Burma campaign had a psychological impact on the British forces. The British were shocked that Indian soldiers had turned against them, undermining their confidence in maintaining control over India. The INA also had a significant impact on the Indian independence movement. Bose’s vision of a socialist India with equal rights for all citizens inspired many Indians. The INA became a symbol of the struggle against British colonialism, and Bose’s slogan of ‘Jai Hind’ became a rallying cry for the independence movement.
However, the INA’s military campaigns were not successful in achieving their goal of freeing India from British rule. The INA suffered significant losses in battles, and their efforts were undermined by the Japanese surrender in 1945.
What was the primary reason for the Japanese to support Subhas Chandra Bose and the formation of the INA?

They were looking for allies in their fight against the British Empire.
They believed in Bose’s vision of a communist India.
They wanted to expand their influence in Southeast Asia.

The passage mentions that the Japanese were interested in having Bose’s help in their own efforts to expand their influence in Southeast Asia, which is why they supported the formation of the Indian National Army (INA).

The primary reason for the Japanese to support Subhas Chandra Bose and the formation of the INA was:

They wanted to expand their influence in Southeast Asia.

Thus, Option (d) is the right answer.

Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.
Algae are photosynthetic creatures that have pigments that aid in photosynthesis, such as chlorophyll. They do not, however, have the actual stems, roots or leaves found in vascular plants. While some of them have many cells, others are unicellular. They might establish colonies as well. The majority of algae are aquatic. Some are terrestrial, and they can be found on rocks, trees and moist soil. Certain algae species coexist well with other living things. For instance, lichens are a symbiotic relationship between green (and often blue-green) algae and fungi. Algae are members of a multiphyletic group. This indicates that there is no common ancestor and that the species in this category are not necessarily closely related. They do not have other morphoanatomical characteristics typical of vascular plants, but they do have one thing in common: they are eukaryotes with the principal pigment being chlorophyll, which allows them to perform photosynthesis. Phycology is the scientific name for the study of algae. The blue-green algae is one example of a reference. But some sources do not classify them as algae because they are prokaryotes.

No common ancestor, not closely related

Algae are photosynthetic creatures that have pigments that aid in photosynthesis, such as chlorophyll. They do not, however, have the actual stems, roots or leaves found in vascular plants. The extraction of indigo dye involves harvesting the small, green leaves of the Indigofera plant before its flowers bloom. These leaves undergo a process of soaking in water and churning until a navy blue froth is released. The upper portion of the resulting mixture is drained for irrigation, while the leaves are repurposed as fertilizer. After allowing the water and fine sediment to settle for a day, the liquid is separated from the sediment. The obtained deep blue paste is then subjected to filtration to remove dirt and impurities, followed by compression into cakes and drying for several days. Once dried, the indigo is ready for use as a dye. The extraction of indigo dye involves harvesting the small, green leaves of the Indigofera plant before its flowers bloom. These leaves undergo a process of soaking in water and churning until a navy blue froth is released. The upper portion of the resulting mixture is drained for irrigation, while the leaves are repurposed as fertilizer. After allowing the water and fine sediment to settle for a day, the liquid is separated from the sediment. expl:

The corrected sentence would be: "You, she, and I have been working happily in the same company and in the same branch for the last nine years."

Influence refers to the ability to have an effect on others, but it is broader and doesn’t specifically capture the personal allure or charm implied by charisma.

Thus, Option (c) is the right answer.

qhtml:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part which contains a grammatical error.
If there is no error in the sentence, then select 'No Error'.
The company will invest more(A) six hundred crores(B) in the next five years to expand(C) its operations in Britain (D).
expl:
⚠️ Note: the official key marks option (a) (part A), and that is the intended error; strictly, part B also has a slip — after a number crore stays singular (six hundred crore), so the sentence carries a second, minor error.

Rule: more comparing an amount with a figure must be followed by than (से अधिक).

Example: She scored more than 90 marks.

Without than, more six hundred crores says nothing.

Correct it.

The company will invest more than six hundred crore in the next five years to expand its operations in Britain.

Answer: A

Why the others are fine.

• C — in the next five years to expand — in the next five years is the right time phrase; to expand is an infinitive of purpose (उद्देश्य बताने वाला infinitive).

• D — its operations in Britain — its (no apostrophe) is the possessive that matches the singular company (एकवचन सर्वनाम).

The second slip in B.

After a definite number, hundred, thousand, lakh, crore, million, dozen stay singular: six hundred crore, five lakh, two dozen (संख्या के बाद crore एकवचन).

The plural is used only without a number: crores of rupees.

More … than: a comparison is not complete without “than”.

qhtml:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:
Pride and Prejudice by Jane Austen is a classic known for its humor and complex characters. The famous first sentence of the book, "It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife," begins to set up all of the major themes of money, status, and marrying well that are prevalent in 19th-century England. The Bennet family, particularly Elizabeth Bennet, a smart and strong-willed heroine, is the subject of Austen’s commentary on the societal imperative for women to marry well and thereby have a stable income.
The title itself is quite meaningful, as it first indicates the character flaws that drive much of the conflict in this novel, namely Darcy’s pride and Elizabeth’s prejudice. In fact, Mr. Fitzwilliam Darcy, being a rich and high-ranking person, first of all shows a haughty character, thereby being very superior by virtue of his class. Elizabeth, having been offended by his initial lack of warmth, as well as having been misled by the deceiving Mr. Wickham, very quickly showed prejudice against him.
Traces the story of each as they navigate these weaknesses. Darcy needs to lower his pride to appreciate the value of Elizabeth’s inferior standing, though she must see the strength of his superior qualities.
Austen employs irony and satire liberally to point out the absurdities of the class structure. Personages like the obsequious Mr. Collins and the imperious Lady Catherine de Bourgh symbolize the hard and silly aspects of class consciousness. The sojourn at Darcy’s grand estate, Pemberley, is an important defining instance in which the splendor of the property and the favorable reports of his servants compel Elizabeth to revise her earlier opinion and realize the truth of Darcy’s goodness.
In the final analysis, the novel promotes love marriages, couples like Jane and Bingley, and Elizabeth and Darcy, who have successful marriages because of love, in contrast to couples who marry for convenience (Charlotte Collins and Mr. Collins) or those who are full of passion but irresponsible (Lydia and Wickham).
How is the character of Lady Catherine de Bourgh employed in the novel as a criticism of society?
opts: She represents social tyranny and class prejudice.
She is purely comic relief and has no other significance.
She symbolizes ideal maternal love and wisdom.
She represents the struggle of the working class against the landed gentry.
expl:
The deciding line.

"Austen employs irony and satire liberally to point out the absurdities of the class structure. Personages like the obsequious Mr. Collins and the imperious Lady Catherine de Bourgh symbolize the hard and silly aspects of class consciousness."

Read the clue word.

imperious = domineering, expecting others to obey (रौबदार, हुक्म चलाने वाली).

An imperious aristocrat who stands for the "hard" side of class consciousness represents social tyranny and class prejudice (सामाजिक तानाशाही और वर्गीय पूर्वाग्रह).

Why the others are wrong.

• purely comic relief and has no other significance = only there for laughs (केवल हास्य के लिए, और कोई महत्व नहीं) — she is funny, but the passage says she symbolizes something, so "no other significance" is false.

• ideal maternal love and wisdom = a perfect, caring mother figure (आदर्श मातृ-प्रेम और विवेक) — "imperious" is the opposite of tender.

• struggle of the working class against the landed gentry = workers fighting landowners (ज़मींदार वर्ग के विरुद्ध श्रमिक वर्ग का संघर्ष) — she is herself landed aristocracy; she enforces class, she does not fight it.

Word help.

satire = criticism through mockery (व्यंग्य).

obsequious = too eager to please (चापलूस).

Answer: (1) She represents social tyranny and class prejudice.

In RC, "purely … no other significance" is an extreme option — it is almost always the trap.

opts: Arrogance of Lady Catherine and Mr. Collins’s servility

Choose the appropriate antonym of the given word.
Gullibility
expl:
Meaning: gullibility = readiness to believe anything; being easily fooled (भोलापन, जल्दी विश्वास कर लेना).

skepticism = a doubting attitude; not accepting claims without proof (संदेहवाद, शंकालुता) — the opposite.

Answer: Skepticism

Why the others are wrong.

• innocence = freedom from guilt; simplicity (मासूमियत, निर्दोषता) — close to gullibility, not opposite.

• trust = firm belief in someone's honesty (विश्वास) — leans the same way as gullibility.

• Naviety (as printed; correct spelling naivety) = lack of experience or judgement (भोलापन, नादानी) — a synonym.

A gull believes; a skeptic doubts.

qhtml:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:
"Bank failures raise serious concerns about supervisory oversight." The case studies of Credit Suisse and Silicon Valley Bank highlight the deficiencies in supervisory supervision. In many instances, supervisors are hesitant to come into conflict with bank management when weaknesses are identified, preferring to do nothing rather than take corrective action at a point in time when key issues are building into a problem.
Regulators must adopt an attitude change in which they place more emphasis on the results rather than the details. Overemphasis on trivial matters might lead regulators to overlook more fundamental issues, such as whether financial institutions have adequate capital in case of a shock. Regulating requirements must be simplified. Complex regulation requirements in relation to capital may overlook systemic risk in their approaches when stress tests result in activities gravitating towards less heavily regulated institutions in the non-bank sector.
Improved supervisory and bank communications would promote better supervision as a tool for managing risk. Recommendations include being up front about supervisory goals, openness to change within the bank organization, and increased transparency in supervisory contracts as a way of promoting swift problem resolution. These would aid shareholders as well as the overall economy. In conclusion, rather than pursuing a micro-management strategy, a move towards a clearly defined regulation that supports positive incentives is what is needed to ensure that banks behave within frameworks that promote financial stability.
The tone with which the author approaches the current situation of "complex regulation" is best described as:
opts: Impressed by how much attention supervisors pay to tiny details.
Uninterested in how these rules change where money is stored.
Hopeful that it will eventually help find hidden money problems.
Critical because complicated rules can actually cause more risk.
expl:
The deciding lines.

"Regulating requirements must be simplified."

"Complex regulation requirements in relation to capital may overlook systemic risk …"

Read the attitude.

"must be simplified" is a demand for change, and "overlook systemic risk" is a charge against complex rules.

So the author is critical (आलोचनात्मक), because complicated rules can actually let risk grow (जटिल नियम वास्तव में जोखिम बढ़ा सकते हैं).

Why the others are wrong.

• Impressed by attention to tiny details (बारीकियों पर ध्यान से प्रभावित) — the author calls it "overemphasis on trivial matters".

• Uninterested in where money is stored (उदासीन) — the author specifically worries that activity shifts to the non-bank sector.

• Hopeful that it will help find hidden problems (आशावान) — the author says it overlooks risk, not that it finds it.

Word help.

trivial = unimportant (तुच्छ, मामूली).

overemphasis = too much stress on something (अत्यधिक ज़ोर).

Answer: (4) Critical because complicated rules can actually cause more risk.

"Must be simplified" is a verdict — a neutral or hopeful tone cannot sit beside it.

What kind of marriage does Jane Austen appear to prize the most, according to the conclusion of the novel?
opts: Marriage contracts entered into by reason of romantic love alone
Marriages for convenience and connections to family
Based on mutual respect, love, and understanding in marriage
expl:
The deciding line.

"In the final analysis, the novel promotes love marriages … who have successful marriages because of love, in contrast to couples who marry for convenience … or those who are full of passion but irresponsible (Lydia and Wickham)."

Read the contrast.

Austen rejects two kinds of marriage: one with no love (convenience), and one with love but no sense (Lydia and Wickham).

What she prizes is love joined with judgement — Darcy lowering his pride and Elizabeth seeing his worth.

That is a marriage of mutual respect, love and understanding (परस्पर सम्मान, प्रेम और आपसी समझ पर आधारित विवाह).

Why the others are wrong.

• romantic love alone = love without anything else (केवल रोमानी प्रेम) — passion alone is exactly what Lydia and Wickham had, and the passage calls them irresponsible.

• for convenience and connections to family = marrying for practical gain or family ties (सुविधा और पारिवारिक संबंधों के लिए विवाह) — this is Charlotte and Mr. Collins, the couple Austen sets in contrast.

• based solely on financial security = marrying only for money (केवल आर्थिक सुरक्षा पर आधारित विवाह) — the same "convenience" model; "solely" rules it out at once.

Word help.

in the final analysis = when everything is considered (अंततः, कुल मिलाकर).

Answer: (4) Based on mutual respect, love, and understanding in marriage

"Love" in option (a) tempts, but "alone" describes Lydia, not Elizabeth.

qhtml:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the one which gives the meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
A stitch in time saves nine
expl:
Meaning: a stitch in time saves nine = fixing a small problem at once stops it from growing and needing much more work later (समय पर किया गया छोटा काम बाद की बड़ी मेहनत बचाता है).

Example: Get that small leak repaired now — a stitch in time saves nine.

Origin.

From sewing: one stitch on a small tear today saves the many stitches a bigger tear would need later; “nine” was chosen partly for the rhyme with time.

Answer: Timely action prevents more work

Why the others are wrong.

• Saving money for the future = to save for a rainy day (बुरे वक्त के लिए बचत).

• Drunk or intoxicated = three sheets to the wind (नशे में धुत).

• Tailoring is a valuable skill — a literal reading of “stitch” (दर्ज़ी का हुनर); the proverb is about timing, not tailoring.

The key word is “time”, not “stitch”.

systemic risk = risk to the whole financial system (प्रणालीगत जोखिम).

non-bank sector = lenders that are not banks (गैर-बैंकिंग क्षेत्र).

Answer: (3) The movement of risk-related financial activities into industries that are less heavily regulated.

Squeeze risk in one place and it moves to another — it does not disappear.

Improved supervisory and bank communications would promote better supervision as a tool for managing risk. Recommendations include being up front about supervisory goals, openness to change within the bank organization, and increased transparency in supervisory contracts as a way of promoting swift problem resolution. These would aid shareholders as well as the overall economy. In conclusion, rather than pursuing a micro-management strategy, a move towards a clearly defined regulation that supports positive incentives is what is needed to ensure that banks behave within frameworks that promote financial stability.
stem: The use of "stress tests" by the author is an example of illustrating which of the following consequences?

Earlier: "The value of the rupee dropped when oil prices climbed".

Given below are four jumbled parts of a sentence. Select the option that gives their correct order.
A) has been attributed by many climate scientists
B) the unprecedented frequency of extreme weather events
C) to the steady rise in global atmospheric temperatures
D) observed across various continents over the last decade
expl:
Rule: in a jumbled sentence, find the subject first, then the words that describe it, then the verb, then whatever the verb's preposition demands.

Find the subject.

B — the unprecedented frequency of extreme weather events — a noun phrase starting with the; it is the only part that can open.

Describe it.

D — observed across various continents over the last decade — a past-participle phrase that tells us which events; it sits right after B.

The verb.

A — has been attributed by many climate scientists — singular has agrees with frequency.

Close with the complement.

The pattern is attribute X to Y, so C — to the steady rise in global atmospheric temperatures — ends the sentence.

The sentence.

The unprecedented frequency of extreme weather events observed across various continents over the last decade has been attributed by many climate scientists to the steady rise in global atmospheric temperatures.

unprecedented = never happened before (अभूतपूर्व).

attributed to = said to be caused by (का कारण माना गया).

Attribute takes “to”: an effect is attributed to its cause.

Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:
The Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act (VB-GRAM G), 2025, has been replaced by the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA). The goal of this modification is to improve Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, which protects the right to life. MGNREGA has improved socioeconomic conditions by facilitating wage payments, providing unemployment benefits, and promoting equal earnings. There has been sustainable development, and research has confirmed the impact of this program to raise earnings, alleviate poverty, and encourage school enrollment. In the past five years, women have comprised 58% of the workforce, significantly contributing to rural development, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic. Given these factors, it is important to assess both the benefits and current challenges of the system.
Despite MGNREGA’s successes, the program has faced implementation challenges, mainly due to inadequate funding, as acknowledged by the Ministry of Finance. Delays in wage payments and fewer work opportunities have resulted from this lack of funds. Recent rules, such as introducing an attendance application that uses photos, have created new problems and made corruption easier. Due to these issues, the VB-GRAM G Act has introduced important changes, including sections 5(1) and 4(5), which give the Union Government greater control over the public works program.
What might be the author’s overall purpose for discussing the development from MGNREGA to the VB-GRAM G Act?
opts: Emphasize how institutional reforms try to maintain constitutionally provided rights while recognizing administrative weaknesses
Argue that a decrease in the role of government can logically solve the inherent shortcomings in rural employment patterns
Argue that a transition from a rights-based framework to an AI-based system is necessary to achieve efficient results for rural communities.
Argue that technology-based interventions will necessarily increase the levels of transparency and accountability associated with public programs
expl:
The deciding lines.

Paragraph 1: "The goal of this modification is to improve Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, which protects the right to life."

Paragraph 2: "the program has faced implementation challenges, mainly due to inadequate funding … Due to these issues, the VB-GRAM G Act has introduced important changes".

Join the two halves.

Half 1 — the reform protects a constitutional right (संवैधानिक अधिकार).

Half 2 — the author openly lists administrative weaknesses (प्रशासनिक कमज़ोरियाँ): fund shortage, wage delays, corruption.

Option (a) says exactly this: reforms try to keep constitutional rights while admitting administrative weakness (संस्थागत सुधार संवैधानिक अधिकार बनाए रखने का प्रयास करते हैं और प्रशासनिक कमियाँ भी स्वीकार करते हैं).

Why the others are wrong.

• a decrease in the role of government (सरकार की भूमिका घटाना) — the opposite: the new Act gives the Union Government greater control.

• from a rights-based framework to an AI-based system (अधिकार-आधारित ढाँचे से AI-आधारित व्यवस्था की ओर) — AI is never mentioned, and the Article 21 link keeps it rights-based.

• technology will necessarily increase transparency (तकनीक से पारदर्शिता अनिवार्य रूप से बढ़ेगी) — the passage says the photo app made corruption easier.

Word help.

alleviate = to reduce, ease (कम करना).

Article 21 = right to life and personal liberty (जीवन और व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार).

Note on the passage: its first sentence is worded backwards — in fact the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 replaced MGNREGA; no question in this set depends on that.

Answer: (1) Emphasize how institutional reforms try to maintain constitutionally provided rights while recognizing administrative weaknesses

A purpose question wants both paragraphs — the right option carries the "benefit" and the "weakness" together.

qhtml:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.
He inquired whether the boy's name was Ahmed.
opts: He asked, “Whether the boy's name was Ahmed?”
expl:
Rule: indirect yes/no question → direct speech (अप्रत्यक्ष से प्रत्यक्ष कथन):

• inquired → asked + comma + quotation marks

• drop whether; put the helping verb before the subject and end with ?

• undo the backshift: past was → present is

Example: She asked if I was busy. → She asked, “Are you busy?”

Apply it.

whether the boy's name was Ahmed → Is the boy's name Ahmed?

Answer: He asked, “Is the boy's name Ahmed?”

Why the others are wrong.

• The boy's name is Ahmed? — statement order with a question mark; a direct question puts the helping verb first (प्रश्नवाचक क्रम).

• Whether the boy's name was Ahmed? — whether is only the linker of indirect speech and never goes inside quotes (अप्रत्यक्ष कथन का संयोजक).

• Was the boy's name Ahmed? — the tense is not reversed; the reported was came from a present is (काल वापस नहीं बदला).

Going back to direct speech, undo every change: whether goes, order inverts, tense moves forward.

qhtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’.
Come quickly if you will catch the train.
expl:
Rule: a condition about the future takes the simple present in the if-clause, never will.

Will appears in an if-clause only when it means “are willing to” — If you will wait, I'll fetch it.

To say “come quickly, since you intend to catch the train”, English uses if you want to (or if you are to).

Example: Leave now if you want to reach on time.

Apply it.

Come quickly if you want to catch the train.

want to (चाहते हो) gives the intention; catch stays a base verb after to.

Answer: If you want to

Why the others are wrong.

• No improvement — if you will catch puts a future will inside the condition (शर्त वाले उपवाक्य में will नहीं).

• If you have — have catch is ungrammatical; even have to would mean obligation (बाध्यता), not intention.

• If you will have — repeats the will error and adds have before a base verb (दोहरी भूल).

Condition + purpose: “if you want to …”, “if you are to …” — never “if you will …”.

qhtml:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order.
A. Here, the picture-perfect French Quarter and heritage laden Tamil streets blend into one another.
B. Across many metropolitan cities, there exists a visible conflict in how the old and the new coexist.
C. The old and new, like two different worlds, surviving side by side yet never crossing that chasm.
D. However, Puducherry stands as a striking exception, where these very contrasts are celebrated rather than endured.
expl:
Opener test.

B — Across many metropolitan cities — states the general theme with no back-reference: the opener.

A starts with Here (needs a place named before it) and D with However (needs an idea to contrast with); neither can open.

Links.

B → D: However, Puducherry stands as a striking exception — the exception to B's visible conflict; these very contrasts = B's the old and the new.

D → A: Here = Puducherry; A gives the proof — French Quarter and Tamil streets blend into one another.

A → C: C, a verbless closing image, sums up the theme of the old and new as two different worlds.

Test the other B-opener.

BACD puts Here straight after “many metropolitan cities” — there is no single place for Here to point to, and the French Quarter belongs to Puducherry, which is not named until D.

So only BDAC keeps both pointer words (However, Here) attached to what they need.

The paragraph.

Across many metropolitan cities, there exists a visible conflict in how the old and the new coexist. However, Puducherry stands as a striking exception, where these very contrasts are celebrated rather than endured. Here, the picture-perfect French Quarter and heritage laden Tamil streets blend into one another. The old and new, like two different worlds, surviving side by side yet never crossing that chasm.

Answer: BDAC

Word help.

chasm = a deep gap; a wide difference (खाई).

endured = put up with, suffered (सहन किया).

“Here” and “However” never open a paragraph — each needs something before it.

qhtml:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the one which gives the meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
To strain at a gnat and swallow a camel
opts: To fuss over trifles while ignoring big issues
expl:
Meaning: to strain at a gnat and swallow a camel = to fuss over tiny, unimportant matters while accepting or ignoring something big and serious (छोटी बातों पर बाल की खाल निकालना और बड़ी गलती को अनदेखा करना).

Example: He checked every comma in the contract but signed away the land itself — straining at a gnat and swallowing a camel.

Origin.

From the Bible (Matthew 23:24).

Strict Pharisees strained their wine through cloth so as not to swallow a gnat (a tiny unclean insect), yet ignored the weightier duties of justice and mercy — “swallowing a camel”.

Answer: To fuss over trifles while ignoring big issues

Why the others are wrong.

• meticulous in everything = careful about every detail (हर बात में अत्यंत सावधान) — the idiom mocks misplaced care; all-round care is to dot the i's and cross the t's.

• extremely physically weak = as weak as a kitten (बहुत कमज़ोर).

• a very large appetite = to eat like a horse (बहुत ज़्यादा खाना).

Word help.

gnat = a tiny flying insect (मच्छर जैसा छोटा कीट).

Gnat = trifle, camel = the big issue: strict about the small, blind to the large.

The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part which contains a grammatical error.
If there is no error in the sentence, then select 'No Error'.
The whole family (A)/ would burst into (B)/ peals for laughter. (C)/ No Error (D)
expl:
Rule: peal = a loud, ringing burst of sound; it takes of: peals of laughter (ठहाके), a peal of bells, a peal of thunder.

Example: The joke drew peals of laughter from the class.

Correct it.

The whole family would burst into peals of laughter.

Answer: C

Why the others are fine.

• A — The whole family — a collective noun used as one unit; fine as subject (समूहवाचक संज्ञा).

• B — would burst into — would shows a past habit (भूतकाल की आदत); burst into = suddenly begin (laughter, tears, song) (अचानक … पड़ना).

• D — No Error — cannot be chosen, since part C has an error.

Peals of laughter, peal of bells, clap of thunder — “of” every time.

qhtml:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.
I asked Mary if she would lend me a pencil.
opts: I said, “Mary, will you lend me a pencil?”
I said, “Mary, will she lend me a pencil?”
I asked to Mary, “Would you lend me a pencil?”
I said to Mary, “Can you lent me a pencil?”
expl:
Rule: indirect question → direct speech (अप्रत्यक्ष से प्रत्यक्ष कथन):

• asked → said to — or put the listener first inside the quotes: I said, “Mary, …”

• drop if/whether; use question order and end with ?

• the person spoken to becomes you: she (Mary) → you

• reverse the tense: would → will

Example: He asked me if I was ready. → He said to me, “Are you ready?”

Apply it.

asked Mary → I said, “Mary, …”

if she would lend → will you lend

me → me (the speaker is “I” in both forms)

Answer: I said, “Mary, will you lend me a pencil?”

Why the others are wrong.

• will she lend — Mary is being spoken to, so inside the quotes she must be you — wrong pronoun (सर्वनाम की भूल).

• asked to Mary — ask takes its object directly, never with to (ask के बाद to नहीं आता); would is also left unreversed.

• Can you lent — after a modal the verb stays in base form lend, not past lent (modal के बाद मूल क्रिया); can also changes would/will into ability.

Inside the quotes, the person being addressed is always “you”.

Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:
The Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act (VB-GRAM G), 2025, has been replaced by the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA). The goal of this modification is to improve Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, which protects the right to life. MGNREGA has improved socioeconomic conditions by facilitating wage payments, providing unemployment benefits, and promoting equal earnings. There has been sustainable development, and research has confirmed the impact of this program to raise earnings, alleviate poverty, and encourage school enrollment. In the past five years, women have comprised 58% of the workforce, significantly contributing to rural development, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic. Given these factors, it is important to assess both the benefits and current challenges of the system.
Despite MGNREGA’s successes, the program has faced implementation challenges, mainly due to inadequate funding, as acknowledged by the Ministry of Finance. Delays in wage payments and fewer work opportunities have resulted from this lack of funds. Recent rules, such as introducing an attendance application that uses photos, have created new problems and made corruption easier. Due to these issues, the VB-GRAM G Act has introduced important changes, including sections 5(1) and 4(5), which give the Union Government greater control over the public works program.
The author’s tone regarding new rules (e.g., photo-based attendance) is best described as?
opts: Cautiously critical, admitting the benefits of innovation while pointing out the dangers of abuse in bureaucracies
Detachedly descriptive, outlining reforms to procedures without evaluative judgments.
Digital interventions will resolve longstanding governance issues.
It is a direct rejection that states tech solutions do not work in rural welfare activities because the officials are illiterate
expl:
The deciding line.

"Recent rules, such as introducing an attendance application that uses photos, have created new problems and made corruption easier."

Read the judging words.

"created new problems", "made corruption easier" — the author is clearly critical (आलोचनात्मक).

But the criticism is limited to these particular rules; there is no blanket attack on technology or on officials.

Measured criticism of a specific step = cautiously critical (सावधानीपूर्वक आलोचनात्मक), pointing out the danger of abuse (दुरुपयोग का ख़तरा).

Why the others are wrong.

• Detachedly descriptive, without evaluative judgments (तटस्थ वर्णनात्मक, बिना किसी मूल्यांकन के) — "made corruption easier" is itself a judgement.

• Digital interventions will resolve longstanding governance issues (डिजिटल उपाय पुरानी शासन-समस्याएँ हल कर देंगे) — this is not even a tone, and it is the reverse of what the author says.

• a direct rejection … because the officials are illiterate (अधिकारियों की निरक्षरता के कारण सीधा अस्वीकार) — literacy is never mentioned, and "do not work" is far stronger than the passage.

Word help.

implementation = putting a plan into action (कार्यान्वयन).

tone = the author’s attitude to the subject (लहजा, दृष्टिकोण).

Answer: (1) Cautiously critical, admitting the benefits of innovation while pointing out the dangers of abuse in bureaucracies

Tone questions: find the judging words first, then pick the option of the same strength — not stronger, not weaker.

Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:
Pride and Prejudice by Jane Austen is a classic known for its humor and complex characters. The famous first sentence of the book, "It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife," begins to set up all of the major themes of money, status, and marrying well that are prevalent in 19th-century England. The Bennet family, particularly Elizabeth Bennet, a smart and strong-willed heroine, is the subject of Austen’s commentary on the societal imperative for women to marry well and thereby have a stable income.
The title itself is quite meaningful, as it first indicates the character flaws that drive much of the conflict in this novel, namely Darcy’s pride and Elizabeth’s prejudice. In fact, Mr. Fitzwilliam Darcy, being a rich and high-ranking person, first of all shows a haughty character, thereby being very superior by virtue of his class. Elizabeth, having been offended by his initial lack of warmth, as well as having been misled by the deceiving Mr. Wickham, very quickly showed prejudice against him.
Traces the story of each as they navigate these weaknesses. Darcy needs to lower his pride to appreciate the value of Elizabeth’s inferior standing, though she must see the strength of his superior qualities.
Austen employs irony and satire liberally to point out the absurdities of the class structure. Personages like the obsequious Mr. Collins and the imperious Lady Catherine de Bourgh symbolize the hard and silly aspects of class consciousness. The sojourn at Darcy’s grand estate, Pemberley, is an important defining instance in which the splendor of the property and the favorable reports of his servants compel Elizabeth to revise her earlier opinion and realize the truth of Darcy’s goodness.
In the final analysis, the novel promotes love marriages, couples like Jane and Bingley, and Elizabeth and Darcy, who have successful marriages because of love, in contrast to couples who marry for convenience (Charlotte Collins and Mr. Collins) or those who are full of passion but irresponsible (Lydia and Wickham).
What are the major themes expressed by the first line of the novel?
expl:
The deciding line.

The first sentence "begins to set up all of the major themes of money, status, and marrying well".

Match it to the options.

money = wealth

status = status

marrying well = marriage

So the themes are wealth, status and marriage (धन, सामाजिक प्रतिष्ठा और विवाह).

Why the others are wrong.

• Education and morality = learning and right conduct (शिक्षा और नैतिकता) — neither idea appears in the line about the opening sentence.

• Nature and the countryside = landscape and rural life (प्रकृति और ग्रामीण परिवेश) — the passage says nothing about scenery.

• Love & War = romance and conflict (प्रेम और युद्ध) — there is no war here, and the opening line is about money and a wife, not romance.

Word help.

universally acknowledged = accepted by everyone (सर्वमान्य).

societal imperative = a duty society forces on people (सामाजिक अनिवार्यता).

Answer: (4) Wealth, status, and marriage

"A single man with a good fortune must want a wife" — money, rank and marriage packed into one sentence.

The Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act (VB-GRAM G), 2025, has been replaced by the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA). The goal of this modification is to improve Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, which protects the right to life. MGNREGA has improved socioeconomic conditions by facilitating wage payments, providing unemployment benefits, and promoting equal earnings. There has been sustainable development, and research has confirmed the impact of this program to raise earnings, alleviate poverty, and encourage school enrollment. In the past five years, women have comprised 58% of the workforce, significantly contributing to rural development, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic. Given these factors, it is important to assess both the benefits and current challenges of the system.
Despite MGNREGA’s successes, the program has faced implementation challenges, mainly due to inadequate funding, as acknowledged by the Ministry of Finance. Delays in wage payments and fewer work opportunities have resulted from this lack of funds. Recent rules, such as introducing an attendance application that uses photos, have created new problems and made corruption easier. Due to these issues, the VB-GRAM G Act has introduced important changes, including sections 5(1) and 4(5), which give the Union Government greater control over the public works program.
What does the author’s discussion of lack of funding primarily indicate?
opts: Local administrations limit opportunities so as to have control over the release of finances.
Administrative inefficiencies and implementation challenges due to a shortage of funding.
Resource allocation practices are highly effective but seem problematic due to certain short-term fiscal fluctuations
Decentralized authority has caused divergent effects that will certainly lead to a reduction in job guarantees.
expl:
The deciding lines.

"the program has faced implementation challenges, mainly due to inadequate funding, as acknowledged by the Ministry of Finance."

"Delays in wage payments and fewer work opportunities have resulted from this lack of funds."

Read what the funding point shows.

Shortage of money → delays and fewer jobs → the scheme is run less efficiently.

That is administrative inefficiency and implementation challenges due to a shortage of funding (धन की कमी से उत्पन्न प्रशासनिक अक्षमता और कार्यान्वयन की चुनौतियाँ).

Why the others are wrong.

• Local administrations limit opportunities to control finances (स्थानीय प्रशासन वित्त पर नियंत्रण के लिए जानबूझकर अवसर घटाते हैं) — no motive is given; the shortfall is admitted by the Ministry of Finance.

• Resource allocation practices are highly effective (संसाधन-आवंटन अत्यंत प्रभावी है) — the passage calls funding inadequate.

• Decentralized authority … will certainly reduce job guarantees (विकेंद्रीकृत अधिकार से रोज़गार गारंटी निश्चित रूप से घटेगी) — the passage speaks of more central control, and "certainly" is too strong.

Word help.

inadequate = not enough (अपर्याप्त).

acknowledged = admitted as true (स्वीकार किया).

Answer: (2) Administrative inefficiencies and implementation challenges due to a shortage of funding.

The right option here reuses the passage’s own nouns — "implementation challenges", "funding".

qhtml:
In the following question, some of the words in the passage have been left out. Read the passage carefully and choose the correct word for each blank, out of the four alternatives and fill in the blanks.
After falling consistently (1) ______ the U.S. dollar for a major part of the year, the rupee has (2) ______ somewhat over the last few weeks. It has risen by almost 5% from its lowest levels (3) ______ in October. Even with this recent improvement, the rupee is still down about 11% since the start of the year. The rupee’s performance has been closely (4) ______ to global crude oil prices. This makes sense, as imported oil accounts for about 80% of India’s total demand. The value of the rupee dropped when oil prices climbed earlier this year, a trend that lasted until early October. Since then, as global crude prices have fallen, the rupee has (5) ______ against the dollar.
What should come in blank (1) ?
expl:
Rule: one currency rises or falls against another — against = measured in comparison with (के मुकाबले).

Example: The yen fell against the euro this week.

The deciding words.

"After falling consistently [blank] the U.S. dollar"

The passage itself confirms the pattern at the end: "the rupee has strengthened against the dollar".

Why the others are wrong.

• with = together with (के साथ) — "falling with the dollar" would mean both fell together.

• of = belonging to (का) — "falling of the dollar" makes no sense here.

• for = for the sake of (के लिए) — gives a purpose, not a comparison.

Word help.

consistently = steadily, without a break (लगातार).

Answer: (1) against

Currencies always move "against" each other — fall against, rise against, strengthen against.

Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’.
Tom was standing besides the schoolhouse poster, when the ball rolled towards him.
expl:
Rule: beside = next to, at the side of (के पास, बगल में).

besides = in addition to, moreover (के अलावा).

Example: She sat beside me. Besides English, he speaks French.

Position by a poster needs beside.

was standing (past continuous) is right — an action in progress when another action (the ball rolled) happened.

Answer: standing beside the schoolhouse poster

Why the others are wrong.

• No improvement — keeps besides, which means “in addition to”, not “next to”.

• stand beside — was stand is ungrammatical; was needs the -ing form here (was के बाद ing रूप).

• stood beside — was stood puts a past form after was; for an action in progress use was standing (was के साथ V2 नहीं).

Beside = by the side; besides = plus — the extra “s” adds.

After falling consistently (1) ______ the U.S. dollar for a major part of the year, the rupee has (2) ______ somewhat over the last few weeks. It has risen by almost 5% from its lowest levels (3) ______ in October. Even with this recent improvement, the rupee is still down about 11% since the start of the year. The rupee’s performance has been closely (4) ______ to global crude oil prices. This makes sense, as imported oil accounts for about 80% of India’s total demand. The value of the rupee dropped when oil prices climbed earlier this year, a trend that lasted until early October. Since then, as global crude prices have fallen, the rupee has (5) ______ against the dollar.
What should come in blank (4) ?
expl:
Rule: after has been + adverb, the sentence needs a participle or adjective — His fate has been closely linked to hers.

The fixed collocation is closely tied to = closely connected with (से गहराई से जुड़ा हुआ).

The deciding words.

"The rupee’s performance has been closely [blank] to global crude oil prices. This makes sense, as imported oil accounts for about 80% of India’s total demand."

The next sentence gives the reason for the link — so the blank means "connected".

Why the others are wrong.

• tightly = firmly (कसकर) — an adverb; "closely tightly" stacks two adverbs with no verb.

• amicably = in a friendly way (मैत्रीपूर्ण ढंग से) — an adverb, and friendship makes no sense for prices.

• morally = in terms of right and wrong (नैतिक रूप से) — an adverb, and morality is irrelevant.

Word help.

accounts for = makes up, forms (का हिस्सा बनाता है).

Answer: (3) tied

Three adverbs and one participle — after "closely", only the participle can stand.

qhtml:
Choose the option that contains the homonym of the highlighted word in the given sentence.
Please make sure to write your full home address, including the apartment number and zip code, on the top of the application form.
opts: After living in the city for ten years, Sarah had to notify the post office that her permanent address was changing to a rural farmhouse.
Millions of people tuned in to watch the president’s televised address regarding the new economic policies.
The celebrity requested that her residential address be kept private and removed from all public search directories for security reasons.
The delivery driver called me because he was having trouble finding my address on the GPS due to the new construction in the neighborhood.
expl:
Meaning: homonyms = words with the same spelling and sound but different meanings (समरूपी शब्द).

In the stem, address = the details of where someone lives (पता).

In option (b), address = a formal speech to an audience (संबोधन, भाषण) — same word, different meaning.

Answer: Millions of people tuned in to watch the president’s televised address regarding the new economic policies.

Why the others are wrong.

• her permanent address — where she lives (स्थायी पता): the same meaning as the stem.

• her residential address — home location (आवासीय पता): the same meaning.

• my address on the GPS — the location of my home (घर का पता): the same meaning.

address also works as a verb — “address the issue” = deal with it (समाधान करना) — a third sense to remember.

qhtml:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:
The Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act (VB-GRAM G), 2025, has been replaced by the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA). The goal of this modification is to improve Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, which protects the right to life. MGNREGA has improved socioeconomic conditions by facilitating wage payments, providing unemployment benefits, and promoting equal earnings. There has been sustainable development, and research has confirmed the impact of this program to raise earnings, alleviate poverty, and encourage school enrollment. In the past five years, women have comprised 58% of the workforce, significantly contributing to rural development, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic. Given these factors, it is important to assess both the benefits and current challenges of the system.
Despite MGNREGA’s successes, the program has faced implementation challenges, mainly due to inadequate funding, as acknowledged by the Ministry of Finance. Delays in wage payments and fewer work opportunities have resulted from this lack of funds. Recent rules, such as introducing an attendance application that uses photos, have created new problems and made corruption easier. Due to these issues, the VB-GRAM G Act has introduced important changes, including sections 5(1) and 4(5), which give the Union Government greater control over the public works program.
What does "sustainable development" mean most nearly in the context of the passage?
opts: Discusses advancements that are characterized by fast infrastructure development without consideration of administrative viability.
Outcomes that emphasize the creation of jobs in the short term, even if there are uncertain long-term consequences for individual welfare
Strategies that place emphasis mainly on technological diffusion as a principal means of rural transformation
Improvements relating to long-term socioeconomic benefits for rural households via stable program design
expl:
The deciding line.

"MGNREGA has improved socioeconomic conditions … There has been sustainable development, and research has confirmed the impact of this program to raise earnings, alleviate poverty, and encourage school enrollment."

Read the phrase in its sentence.

sustainable = able to last over the long term (दीर्घकालिक, टिकाऊ).

The examples that follow — higher earnings, less poverty, more schooling — are long-term socioeconomic benefits for rural households.

So the phrase means improvements that last, produced by a stable programme (स्थिर कार्यक्रम-संरचना से ग्रामीण परिवारों को मिलने वाले दीर्घकालिक सामाजिक-आर्थिक लाभ).

Why the others are wrong.

• fast infrastructure development without consideration of administrative viability (व्यवहार्यता की परवाह किए बिना तेज़ बुनियादी ढाँचा विकास) — "without consideration" is the opposite of sustainable.

• creation of jobs in the short term, with uncertain long-term consequences (अल्पकालिक रोज़गार, दीर्घकालिक परिणाम अनिश्चित) — "short term" contradicts "sustainable".

• technological diffusion as a principal means (तकनीक के प्रसार को मुख्य साधन मानना) — the passage’s examples are earnings, poverty and schooling, not technology.

Word help.

socioeconomic = relating to both society and money (सामाजिक-आर्थिक).

enrollment = registering as a student (नामांकन).

Answer: (4) Improvements relating to long-term socioeconomic benefits for rural households via stable program design

"Sustainable" always carries "long-term" — any option built on "short-term" or "fast" is out.

In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the one which can be substituted for the given words/sentence.
Fear of ugliness.
expl:
Meaning: cacophobia = an abnormal fear of ugliness (कुरूपता का भय).

Greek kakos = bad, ugly + phobos = fear — the same caco- as in cacophony (an ugly, harsh sound).

Answer: Cacophobia

Why the others are wrong.

• acrophobia = fear of heights (ऊँचाई का भय) — Greek akron = peak.

• arachnophobia = fear of spiders (मकड़ी का भय) — Greek arachne = spider.

• hydrophobia = fear of water (जल का भय) — also an old name for rabies.

caco- = bad or ugly: cacophony (harsh sound), cacography (bad handwriting), cacophobia (fear of ugliness).

qhtml: Select the correctly spelt word out of the four alternatives.
expl:
Meaning: grotesque = strangely ugly or distorted; absurdly odd (विचित्र, विकृत, भद्दा).

Spelling: G-R-O-T-E-S-Q-U-E = grot + the French suffix -esque (“in the style of”), as in picturesque.

Answer: Grotesque

Why the others are wrong.

• Grostasque — an extra s after Gro, and a where e belongs.

• Grosteasque — an extra s and an extra a.

• Growtesque — ow for the single o.

-esque words: picturesque, statuesque, grotesque — one “t”, then “-esque”.
