qhtml:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:
Pride and Prejudice by Jane Austen is a classic known for its humor and complex characters. The famous first sentence of the book, "It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife," begins to set up all of the major themes of money, status, and marrying well that are prevalent in 19th-century England. The Bennet family, particularly Elizabeth Bennet, a smart and strong-willed heroine, is the subject of Austen’s commentary on the societal imperative for women to marry well and thereby have a stable income.
The title itself is quite meaningful, as it first indicates the character flaws that drive much of the conflict in this novel, namely Darcy’s pride and Elizabeth’s prejudice. In fact, Mr. Fitzwilliam Darcy, being a rich and high-ranking person, first of all shows a haughty character, thereby being very superior by virtue of his class. Elizabeth, having been offended by his initial lack of warmth, as well as having been misled by the deceiving Mr. Wickham, very quickly showed prejudice against him.
Traces the story of each as they navigate these weaknesses. Darcy needs to lower his pride to appreciate the value of Elizabeth’s inferior standing, though she must see the strength of his superior qualities.
Austen employs irony and satire liberally to point out the absurdities of the class structure. Personages like the obsequious Mr. Collins and the imperious Lady Catherine de Bourgh symbolize the hard and silly aspects of class consciousness. The sojourn at Darcy’s grand estate, Pemberley, is an important defining instance in which the splendor of the property and the favorable reports of his servants compel Elizabeth to revise her earlier opinion and realize the truth of Darcy’s goodness.
In the final analysis, the novel promotes love marriages, couples like Jane and Bingley, and Elizabeth and Darcy, who have successful marriages because of love, in contrast to couples who marry for convenience (Charlotte Collins and Mr. Collins) or those who are full of passion but irresponsible (Lydia and Wickham).
What is the key event that marks a turning point in making Elizabeth change her view of Darcy?
opts: Her visit to Pemberley and her reception of Darcy’s letter
expl:
The deciding line.

"The sojourn at Darcy’s grand estate, Pemberley, is an important defining instance in which the splendor of the property and the favorable reports of his servants compel Elizabeth to revise her earlier opinion."

Read the clue phrase.

defining instance = the moment that decides the direction of things — a turning point (निर्णायक मोड़).

Only option (b) contains the visit to Pemberley (पेम्बर्ली की यात्रा).

The letter in that option comes from the novel itself: Darcy’s letter after his first proposal exposes Wickham’s lies (डार्सी का पत्र मिलना) and begins the change the Pemberley visit completes.

Why the others are wrong.

• Rejection of Mr. Collins’s Proposal = Elizabeth refusing Collins (मिस्टर कॉलिन्स का विवाह-प्रस्ताव ठुकराना) — it concerns Collins and changes nothing about Darcy.

• Lydia’s elopement with Wickham = Lydia running away with Wickham (लिडिया का विकहम के साथ भाग जाना) — not in the passage; in the novel it comes after her view of Darcy has already softened.

• The Netherfield Ball = a dance party early in the story (नेदरफ़ील्ड का नृत्य-समारोह) — at that stage her dislike of Darcy is still growing.

Word help.

sojourn = a short stay (अल्प-प्रवास).

splendor = grandness (वैभव, भव्यता).

Answer: (2) Her visit to Pemberley and her reception of Darcy’s letter

"Revise her earlier opinion" is the passage’s own way of saying "turning point" — find that phrase and you find the event.

Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:
"Bank failures raise serious concerns about supervisory oversight." The case studies of Credit Suisse and Silicon Valley Bank highlight the deficiencies in supervisory supervision. In many instances, supervisors are hesitant to come into conflict with bank management when weaknesses are identified, preferring to do nothing rather than take corrective action at a point in time when key issues are building into a problem.
Regulators must adopt an attitude change in which they place more emphasis on the results rather than the details. Overemphasis on trivial matters might lead regulators to overlook more fundamental issues, such as whether financial institutions have adequate capital in case of a shock. Regulating requirements must be simplified. Complex regulation requirements in relation to capital may overlook systemic risk in their approaches when stress tests result in activities gravitating towards less heavily regulated institutions in the non-bank sector.
Improved supervisory and bank communications would promote better supervision as a tool for managing risk. Recommendations include being up front about supervisory goals, openness to change within the bank organization, and increased transparency in supervisory contracts as a way of promoting swift problem resolution. These would aid shareholders as well as the overall economy. In conclusion, rather than pursuing a micro-management strategy, a move towards a clearly defined regulation that supports positive incentives is what is needed to ensure that banks behave within frameworks that promote financial stability.
What would "positive incentives" do for the banking system?
opts: Help banks behave in a way that keeps the economy stable.
Stop banks and regulators from talking to each other often.
Make bank rules much more complicated and harder to follow.
Bring back micro-management and focus on tiny details.
expl:
The deciding line.

"a clearly defined regulation that supports positive incentives is what is needed to ensure that banks behave within frameworks that promote financial stability."

Read the phrase.

incentive = a reward that encourages a certain behaviour (प्रोत्साहन).

The same sentence states their purpose: to make banks behave in ways that promote financial stability.

So they help banks act in a way that keeps the economy stable (बैंकों को ऐसा व्यवहार करने में मदद करना जिससे अर्थव्यवस्था स्थिर रहे).

Why the others are wrong.

• Stop banks and regulators from talking often (बैंकों और नियामकों की आपसी बातचीत बंद करना) — the author wants improved communication.

• Make bank rules more complicated (नियमों को और जटिल बनाना) — the author says rules "must be simplified".

• Bring back micro-management (सूक्ष्म-प्रबंधन की वापसी) — rejected in the same sentence: "rather than pursuing a micro-management strategy".

Word help.

framework = a basic structure of rules (ढाँचा).

financial stability = a steady, crisis-free money system (वित्तीय स्थिरता).

Answer: (1) Help banks behave in a way that keeps the economy stable.

The purpose clause "to ensure that …" right after the phrase is the definition the question wants.

Spot the misspelling.

Impetunent is not an English word.

The nearest real word is impertinent = rude, not showing proper respect (धृष्ट, अशिष्ट) — spelt I-M-P-E-R-T-I-N-E-N-T.

Answer: Impetunent

Why the others are fine.

• Impetuous = acting suddenly without thinking (उतावला, आवेगी) — correct spelling, -uous ending.

• Imperial = relating to an empire or emperor (साम्राज्यिक, शाही) — correct.

• Implication = a suggested meaning, or a likely result (निहितार्थ, परिणाम) — correct.

Impetuous (rash) and impertinent (rude) both start “imp-” — learn their middles: -etu- and -ert-.

qhtml:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:
"Bank failures raise serious concerns about supervisory oversight." The case studies of Credit Suisse and Silicon Valley Bank highlight the deficiencies in supervisory supervision. In many instances, supervisors are hesitant to come into conflict with bank management when weaknesses are identified, preferring to do nothing rather than take corrective action at a point in time when key issues are building into a problem.
Regulators must adopt an attitude change in which they place more emphasis on the results rather than the details. Overemphasis on trivial matters might lead regulators to overlook more fundamental issues, such as whether financial institutions have adequate capital in case of a shock. Regulating requirements must be simplified. Complex regulation requirements in relation to capital may overlook systemic risk in their approaches when stress tests result in activities gravitating towards less heavily regulated institutions in the non-bank sector.
Improved supervisory and bank communications would promote better supervision as a tool for managing risk. Recommendations include being up front about supervisory goals, openness to change within the bank organization, and increased transparency in supervisory contracts as a way of promoting swift problem resolution. These would aid shareholders as well as the overall economy. In conclusion, rather than pursuing a micro-management strategy, a move towards a clearly defined regulation that supports positive incentives is what is needed to ensure that banks behave within frameworks that promote financial stability.
Which of the following is most true in regard to stating the structure of logic found in the author’s conclusion?
opts: It proposes that bank managers should be given more freedom in setting.
It suggests a complete deregulation of the banking system to promote a competitive world economy.
It suggests that the responsibility for assurance should lie with organizations rather than with outsiders.
It urges a transition from procedural pedantry towards a results-oriented strategic framework.
expl:
The deciding lines.

"Regulators must adopt an attitude change in which they place more emphasis on the results rather than the details."

"In conclusion, rather than pursuing a micro-management strategy, a move towards a clearly defined regulation that supports positive incentives is what is needed".

Read the structure.

The conclusion moves from X to Y:

X = micro-management, obsession with details = procedural pedantry (प्रक्रियात्मक बारीकियों में उलझे रहना)

Y = clear rules judged by outcomes = a results-oriented strategic framework (परिणाम-केंद्रित रणनीतिक ढाँचा)

Option (d) states exactly this "from … towards …" shape.

Why the others are wrong.

• bank managers should be given more freedom (बैंक प्रबंधकों को अधिक स्वतंत्रता) — the author wants supervisors to confront bank management, not leave it free (the option is even left incomplete: "freedom in setting" what?).

• complete deregulation (बैंकिंग व्यवस्था का पूर्ण विनियमन-मुक्त होना) — the author asks for clearly defined regulation: simpler rules, not no rules.

• responsibility for assurance should lie with organizations rather than outsiders (आश्वासन की ज़िम्मेदारी संस्थाओं पर, बाहरी निगरानीकर्ताओं पर नहीं) — the whole passage is about outside supervisors doing their job better.

Word help.

oversight = supervision (निगरानी).

micro-management = controlling every small detail (हर छोटी बात पर नियंत्रण).

Answer: (4) It urges a transition from procedural pedantry towards a results-oriented strategic framework.

"Rather than X, a move towards Y" is a transition — the answer must name both ends.

qhtml:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.
Why was such a letter written by your brother?
opts: Why was your brother writing such a letter?
Why had your brother written such a letter?
Why does your brother write such a letter?
Why did your brother write such a letter?
expl:
Rule: simple past passive question (सामान्य भूत कर्मवाच्य प्रश्न) → active:

Wh + was/were + object + V3 + by + agent ⇒ Wh + did + subject + V1 + object?

Example: When was the bridge built by them? → When did they build the bridge?

Apply it.

by your brother → subject: your brother

was … written → did … write

object → such a letter

Answer: Why did your brother write such a letter?

Why the others are wrong.

• was … writing — past continuous (अपूर्ण भूत); the passive had no being.

• had … written — past perfect (पूर्ण भूत); the passive had no been.

• does … write — simple present (सामान्य वर्तमान); the passive was is past.

was/were + V3 in a passive question ⇒ did + V1 in the active.

Why are supervisors often slow to act when banks have problems?
opts: They are confused because modern bank rules are too simple.
They do not have the legal power to stop a financial crash.
They use a secret strategy to keep their contracts private.
They prefer to avoid conflict instead of fixing risks early.
expl:
The deciding line.

"supervisors are hesitant to come into conflict with bank management when weaknesses are identified, preferring to do nothing rather than take corrective action at a point in time when key issues are building into a problem."

Paraphrase it.

hesitant to come into conflict = they avoid conflict (टकराव से बचते हैं).

rather than take corrective action early = instead of fixing risks early (जोखिम को समय रहते ठीक करने के बजाय).

Option (d) is a near word-for-word paraphrase.

Why the others are wrong.

• modern bank rules are too simple (बैंक नियम बहुत सरल हैं) — the passage says the rules are too complex.

• no legal power to stop a financial crash (वित्तीय संकट रोकने की कानूनी शक्ति नहीं) — the passage blames hesitation, not lack of power.

• a secret strategy to keep contracts private (अनुबंध गुप्त रखने की छिपी रणनीति) — the passage only asks for more transparency; secrecy is not given as the cause.

Word help.

hesitant = unwilling, slow to act (हिचकिचाने वाला).

corrective action = steps to put a fault right (सुधारात्मक कदम).

Answer: (4) They prefer to avoid conflict instead of fixing risks early.

qhtml:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order.
A. Faced with the high cost and scarcity of Indian indigo; European manufacturers were forced to rely on the woad plant for their dyeing needs.
B. However, cloth dyers still preferred indigo, as it produced a significantly richer and more vibrant blue than woad ever could.
C. Since woad thrived in temperate climates, it was readily available and easily cultivated throughout Europe.
D. Indian indigo was prohibitively expensive, and only meager quantities ever reached European markets.
expl:
Opener test.

D — Indian indigo was prohibitively expensive — introduces the subject and its problem with no back-reference: the opener.

A (Faced with the high cost and scarcity) refers back to a problem already stated; B opens with However; C talks about woad before it has been introduced.

Links.

D → A: high cost and scarcity sums up D's prohibitively expensive and meager quantities; A introduces woad as the substitute.

A → C: Since woad thrived in temperate climates — explains why woad was the easy choice in Europe.

C → B: However — despite woad being easy to get, dyers still preferred indigo for its richer blue.

The paragraph.

Indian indigo was prohibitively expensive, and only meager quantities ever reached European markets. Faced with the high cost and scarcity of Indian indigo; European manufacturers were forced to rely on the woad plant for their dyeing needs. Since woad thrived in temperate climates, it was readily available and easily cultivated throughout Europe. However, cloth dyers still preferred indigo, as it produced a significantly richer and more vibrant blue than woad ever could.

Answer: DACB

Word help.

woad = a European plant whose leaves give a blue dye (नील देने वाला एक यूरोपीय पौधा).

prohibitively = so much that it stops people buying (अत्यधिक, पहुँच से बाहर).

meager = very small in amount (अल्प, नाममात्र).

Problem → forced substitute → why the substitute worked → “However”, the lasting preference.

Choose the appropriate synonym of the given word.
Erroneous
expl:
Meaning: erroneous = wrong, containing a mistake (गलत, त्रुटिपूर्ण).

fallacious = based on a mistaken idea, false (भ्रामक, असत्य) — the same sense.

an erroneous belief = a fallacious belief.

Answer: Fallacious

Why the others are wrong.

• vital = absolutely necessary (अत्यंत आवश्यक) — unrelated.

• right = correct (सही) — the opposite.

• accurate = exact, free from error (सटीक, शुद्ध) — the opposite.

Two options here are antonyms — in a synonym item, strike out the opposites first.

qhtml:
In the following question, some of the words in the passage have been left out. Read the passage carefully and choose the correct word for each blank, out of the four alternatives and fill in the blanks.
After falling consistently (1) ______ the U.S. dollar for a major part of the year, the rupee has (2) ______ somewhat over the last few weeks. It has risen by almost 5% from its lowest levels (3) ______ in October. Even with this recent improvement, the rupee is still down about 11% since the start of the year. The rupee’s performance has been closely (4) ______ to global crude oil prices. This makes sense, as imported oil accounts for about 80% of India’s total demand. The value of the rupee dropped when oil prices climbed earlier this year, a trend that lasted until early October. Since then, as global crude prices have fallen, the rupee has (5) ______ against the dollar.
What should come in blank (2) ?
expl:
Rule: the present perfect is has / have + past participle — She has finished the work.

The deciding words.

"the rupee has [blank] somewhat over the last few weeks. It has risen by almost 5% from its lowest levels".

After falling, it rose again — it regained lost value.

recovered = came back to a better state after a fall (उबरना, सुधार होना); it is a past participle, so it fits after "has".

Why the others are wrong.

• admire = to respect and like (प्रशंसा करना) — a base form cannot follow "has", and the sense is absurd.

• energy = power, strength (ऊर्जा) — a noun, not a verb.

• ground = land, or past participle of grind = to crush (पीसना) — "has ground" means "has crushed"; only "has gained ground" (आगे बढ़ा) would fit.

Word help.

somewhat = to some extent (कुछ हद तक).

Answer: (3) recovered

"Ground" is the trap — the idiom is "gain ground", and the verb "gain" is missing.

qhtml:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:
The Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act (VB-GRAM G), 2025, has been replaced by the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA). The goal of this modification is to improve Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, which protects the right to life. MGNREGA has improved socioeconomic conditions by facilitating wage payments, providing unemployment benefits, and promoting equal earnings. There has been sustainable development, and research has confirmed the impact of this program to raise earnings, alleviate poverty, and encourage school enrollment. In the past five years, women have comprised 58% of the workforce, significantly contributing to rural development, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic. Given these factors, it is important to assess both the benefits and current challenges of the system.
Despite MGNREGA’s successes, the program has faced implementation challenges, mainly due to inadequate funding, as acknowledged by the Ministry of Finance. Delays in wage payments and fewer work opportunities have resulted from this lack of funds. Recent rules, such as introducing an attendance application that uses photos, have created new problems and made corruption easier. Due to these issues, the VB-GRAM G Act has introduced important changes, including sections 5(1) and 4(5), which give the Union Government greater control over the public works program.
What can be reasonably inferred about the relationship between women’s participation and rural resilience during the pandemic?
opts: Their significant involvement contributed to the continuation of the community through the maintenance of the local economy in spite of the general economic disruptions that were happening.
The fact that they were active seemingly led to the acceleration of the community’s fiscal problems because it resulted in program expenditure being amplified during a time of uncertainty.
Their involvement could have led to a decrease in total program productivity owing to the fact that the local populace was heavily burdened with expanded caregiving during the pandemic.
Their intensified appearance might have worsened the existing support structures that were failing in the health crisis.
expl:
The deciding line.

"In the past five years, women have comprised 58% of the workforce, significantly contributing to rural development, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic."

Draw the inference.

More than half the workers were women, and their work contributed most when the pandemic disrupted everything else.

So their participation helped the village economy keep running despite the shock — that is rural resilience (संकट से उबरने की क्षमता).

Option (a) (उनकी बड़ी भागीदारी ने व्यापक आर्थिक व्यवधान के बावजूद स्थानीय अर्थव्यवस्था को चलाए रखा) is the only one in the passage’s direction.

Why the others are wrong.

• accelerated the community’s fiscal problems (समुदाय की वित्तीय समस्याएँ और तेज़ कीं) — the passage calls it a contribution, not a burden.

• decrease in productivity owing to caregiving (देखभाल के बोझ के कारण उत्पादकता में कमी) — caregiving is never mentioned.

• worsened the existing support structures (पहले से कमज़ोर सहायता-तंत्र को और बिगाड़ा) — the opposite of "contributing to rural development".

Word help.

workforce = all the people working (कार्यबल).

comprised = made up (बनाया, गठित किया).

Answer: (1) Their significant involvement contributed to the continuation of the community through the maintenance of the local economy in spite of the general economic disruptions that were happening.

A valid inference stays on the passage’s side — "contributing" can never become "worsened".

qhtml:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.
“Do you suppose you know better than your own father?” jeered his angry mother.
opts: His angry mother jeered and asked whether he had supposed he has known better than his own father.
His angry mother jeered that did he suppose he knew better than his own father.
His angry mother jeered and asked if you suppose you know better than your own father.
His angry mother jeered and asked whether he supposed he knew better than his own father.
expl:
Rule: direct yes/no question → indirect speech (प्रत्यक्ष से अप्रत्यक्ष कथन):

• reporting verb → asked (an extra tone verb is kept: jeered and asked)

• do/does question → whether / if + statement order; no question mark

• pronouns follow the listener: you (the son) → he, your → his

• past reporting verb → each tense goes one step back: suppose → supposed, know → knew

Example: “Are you tired?” she said. → She asked whether I was tired.

Apply it.

Do you suppose → whether he supposed

you know → he knew

your own father → his own father

Answer: His angry mother jeered and asked whether he supposed he knew better than his own father.

Why the others are wrong.

• had supposed … has known — had supposed is past perfect (पूर्ण भूतकाल), one step too far, while has known is not changed at all — the tenses clash.

• that did he suppose — that introduces statements, and did he suppose is still question order; indirect questions use statement order (कथन क्रम).

• if you suppose you know … your — pronouns and tenses left exactly as in the quotes; that is still direct speech (सर्वनाम व काल नहीं बदले).

Word help.

jeered = mocked rudely and loudly (ताना मारा, उपहास किया).

Do/does/did vanish in indirect speech — the main verb carries the tense: “Do you suppose” → “whether he supposed”.

After falling consistently (1) ______ the U.S. dollar for a major part of the year, the rupee has (2) ______ somewhat over the last few weeks. It has risen by almost 5% from its lowest levels (3) ______ in October. Even with this recent improvement, the rupee is still down about 11% since the start of the year. The rupee’s performance has been closely (4) ______ to global crude oil prices. This makes sense, as imported oil accounts for about 80% of India’s total demand. The value of the rupee dropped when oil prices climbed earlier this year, a trend that lasted until early October. Since then, as global crude prices have fallen, the rupee has (5) ______ against the dollar.

expl:
Rule: a past participle can follow a noun as a shortened relative clause — the price paid last year = the price (that was) paid last year.

The deciding words.

= its lowest levels (which it) reached in October.

• admire = to respect and like (प्रशंसा करना) — base form, and levels cannot be admired here.

Answer: (2) reached

Levels, targets and lows are "reached" — the natural verb for a point on a graph.

qhtml:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.
The massive exterior wall of the old mansion was being painted by the skilled laborers when it suddenly started raining heavily.
opts: The skilled laborers painted the massive exterior wall of the old mansion when it suddenly started raining heavily.
The skilled laborers had been painting the massive exterior wall of the old mansion when it suddenly started raining heavily.
The skilled laborers were painting the massive exterior wall of the old mansion when it suddenly started raining heavily.
The skilled laborers are painting the massive exterior wall of the old mansion when it suddenly started raining heavily.
expl:
Rule: past continuous passive (अपूर्ण भूत कर्मवाच्य) → active:

object + was/were being + V3 + by + agent ⇒ agent + was/were + V-ing + object.

The when-clause is a separate clause and stays as it is.

Example: The song was being sung by the girls. → The girls were singing the song.

Apply it.

by the skilled laborers → subject, plural → were

was being painted → were painting

object → the massive exterior wall of the old mansion

Answer: The skilled laborers were painting the massive exterior wall of the old mansion when it suddenly started raining heavily.

Why the others are wrong.

• painted — simple past (सामान्य भूत); being showed an action in progress, which is lost.

• had been painting — past perfect continuous (पूर्ण निरंतर भूतकाल); adds “for some time before”, which the passive did not say.

• are painting — present continuous (अपूर्ण वर्तमान); it clashes with the past started.

Word help.

mansion = a large, grand house (हवेली).

“Being” in a passive is the sign of a continuous tense — keep the -ing in the active.

Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
The burglar destroyed several items in the room. Even the carpet has been torn.
opts: Several items destroyed in the room by the burglar. Even the carpet he has torn.
Including the carpet, several items in the room have been torn by the burglar.
Several items in the room were destroyed by the burglar. Even the carpet has been torn.
The burglar, being destroyed several items in the room, also carpet has torn.
expl:
Rule: simple past active → passive (सामान्य भूत कर्मवाच्य):

subject + V2 + object ⇒ object + was/were + V3 + by + subject.

A sentence that is already passive stays as it is.

Example: The dog bit the boy. → The boy was bitten by the dog.

Sentence 1.

object several items in the room (plural) → were

destroyed → were destroyed by the burglar

Sentence 2.

Even the carpet has been torn — already present perfect passive → unchanged.

Answer: Several items in the room were destroyed by the burglar. Even the carpet has been torn.

Why the others are wrong.

• Several items destroyed … by the burglar — no were before V3, so it is not a passive at all; Even the carpet he has torn turns sentence 2 back into the active (कर्तृवाच्य).

• The burglar, being destroyed — makes the burglar the thing destroyed; ungrammatical and the meaning is reversed (अर्थ उलट गया).

Change only what is active — a sentence already in the passive is left alone.

qhtml:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.
“Call the first witness,” said the judge.
opts: The judge asked if they would call the first witness.
The judge said that the first witness should be called.
The judge ordered them to call the first witness.
The judge ordered that called the first witness.
expl:
Rule: imperative sentence (आज्ञार्थक वाक्य) → indirect speech:

• said → a verb showing the mood: ordered / commanded (command), requested (request), advised (advice)

• add the people addressed as an object — here them

• the imperative verb becomes to + base verb

Example: “Shut the door,” he said to me. → He ordered me to shut the door.

Apply it.

A judge's “Call the first witness” is a command to the court staff.

said → ordered them

Call → to call

Answer: The judge ordered them to call the first witness.

Why the others are wrong.

• asked if they would call — turns the command into a yes/no question (आदेश को प्रश्न बना दिया).

• said that … should be called — reports it as a passive should-clause (कर्मवाच्य); the force of the order and the to-infinitive pattern are lost.

• ordered that called — the that-clause has no subject; ungrammatical (कर्ता ही नहीं).

Command → ordered + object + to + verb.

China and India together will account for more than a third of the estimated global population, which is expected to hit 8.045 billion by mid-year, according to the United Nations Population Fund’s (UNFPA) ‘State of World Population Report’ for 2023. But, contrary to public perception, population growth has been slowing in both countries – particularly in China, which recorded a population decline for the first time in six decades last year.

China’s population fell in 2022 to 1.411 billion, down some 850,000 people from the previous year, according to China’s National Bureau of Statistics (NBS). The birth rate also fell to a record low of 6.77 births per 1,000 people, down from 7.52 a year earlier and the lowest level since the founding of Communist China in 1949.

B. In the next ten years, India’s working-age population will be more than 1 billion.

Both A and B are true

King Sagara, an ancestor of King Bhagiratha, once conducted an ashwamedha yagna to extend his dominion. When the horse went astray, the king sent his 60,000 sons to find the horse. Unfortunately, in the course of the quest, they ended up disrupting the intense meditation of sage Kapila, at whose abode they found the horse. Kapila burnt them all to ashes, sending them all to the netherworld—an act he instantly regretted when he realised what had happened. After breaking the news to King Sagara, he mentioned that the souls of King Sagara’s sons could attain salvation only if the heavenly Ganga could be persuaded to flow over their ashes.

It was Bhagiratha, whose austere penance and devotion pleased Lord Shiva so much so that he persuaded Ganga to descend to the earth. Ganga consented, but the problem arose that the earth would probably be unable to bear the intensity of Ganga’s flow and even be shattered in the process. Thus, a solution was devised: Ganga would first land on Shiva’s head and the locks of his hair would minimise the impact. Still, the force of Ganga’s landing was such that it split into seven tributaries, three of which flowed east and three of them west. The seventh stream followed King Bhagiratha to the place where his ancestor’s ashes lay. The river’s waters instantly purified them. This is also the origin of the belief that the Ganga’s waters can purify mortal souls of all their sins.

In 1888, an Atlantic contributor made the case for a “science of names.”
“Parents are strangely careless and unscientific in giving names to children,” the contributor complained. “They forget that not only from the social point of view it is very advantageous to have one’s name remembered, but that from the business point of view notoriety is capital, and must be obtained by persistent and ingenious advertising.” Indeed, the contributor argued, a good name will give a child “a start in life equivalent to a cash capital of at least fifteen thousand dollars.” One way to ensure this head start? “Be guided by euphonic quality only.”
Although not all of this contributor’s guidance can or should still apply today, the importance of a name to a child’s identity has stayed front of mind for many parents. A name can determine whether a child fits in or stands out—and many parents differ on which of those outcomes is preferable.

expl:
The tone of the speaker in the passage is Persuasive.

While the tone is persuasive, it's important to note that it doesn't necessarily mean the speaker is forcefully imposing a viewpoint. Instead, the speaker seeks to influence the audience's perception by presenting a compelling argument and providing reasons to support the suggested perspective.

Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.
In 1888, an Atlantic contributor made the case for a “science of names.”
“Parents are strangely careless and unscientific in giving names to children,” the contributor complained. “They forget that not only from the social point of view it is very advantageous to have one’s name remembered, but that from the business point of view notoriety is capital, and must be obtained by persistent and ingenious advertising.” Indeed, the contributor argued, a good name will give a child “a start in life equivalent to a cash capital of at least fifteen thousand dollars.” One way to ensure this head start? “Be guided by euphonic quality only.”
Although not all of this contributor’s guidance can or should still apply today, the importance of a name to a child’s identity has stayed front of mind for many parents. A name can determine whether a child fits in or stands out—and many parents differ on which of those outcomes is preferable.

Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.
Leadership does not exist without followership. A leader has to be accepted by the group which the former is supposed to lead. To gain acceptability, the leader should cause an emotive impact on the group members. The strength of character exhibited by leaders makes them dear to their followers. A leader is one who effectively inspires followers to achieve worthwhile things. What character of the leader motivates the followers? It is not pomp and show, neither flattery nor sanctioning more incentives. Pomp and show creates a sense of awe and the leader is deified rather as emulated. Flattery is unrealistic and cannot serve as a long-term motivational tool. A leader’s style should be one that can be emulated by all irrespective of cadre, class and calibre. Simplicity in one’s day- to- day conduct is the only thing that can be adopted by all.
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Emulate
expl:
The most appropriate synonym for the given word "Emulate" is Imitate.

  1. Relax: This word means to become less tense or to loosen up. It does not convey the idea of trying to match or surpass someone's achievements, which is the essence of "emulate."

  2. Imitate: This word is the correct synonym for "emulate." It means to copy or mimic someone's behavior, actions, or achievements with the intention of equaling or surpassing them. In the context of leadership mentioned in the passage, a leader's style should be emulated by followers.

  3. Suppose: This word means to assume or consider something to be true without sufficient evidence. It does not convey the idea of imitating or replicating someone's behavior or achievements.

  4. Exhibit: This word means to display or show something. While it is related to presenting, it doesn't capture the specific idea of imitating or following someone's example, as "emulate" does.

In the context of the passage, the character of a leader that motivates followers is discussed, and the word "emulate" implies followers imitating the leader's style. Therefore, the most appropriate synonym is Imitate.

Taekwondo is a form of empty hand martial arts combat that requires the athlete to use all parts of the body in competition. Taekwondo is a self-defence discipline; the name is derived from the Korean words ‘tae’, meaning kick, ‘kwon’, a punch or other blow with the hand or fist, and ‘do’, which is a way or method of operation. Among the general public, taekwondo is distinguished from other martial arts by its high speed, sweeping kicks and emphatic punches. As with judo, taekwondo was developed as a sport that is also representative of a moral code, where principles of loyalty, faithfulness, respect, and the preservation of an indomitable spirit form a significant part of taekwondo training. Beginning in 1945, shortly after the end of World War II and Japanese Occupation, new martial arts schools called kwans opened in Seoul. These schools were established by Korean martial artists with backgrounds in Japanese and Chinese martial arts. At the time, indigenous disciplines (such as Taekkyeon) were being forgotten, due to years of decline and repression by the Japanese colonial government. The umbrella term traditional Taekwondo typically refers to the martial arts practiced by the kwans during the 1940s and 1950s, though in reality the term ‘Taekwondo’ had not yet been coined at that time, and indeed each kwan (school) was practicing its own unique style of the Korean art.

Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.
Taekwondo is a form of empty hand martial arts combat that requires the athlete to use all parts of the body in competition. Taekwondo is a self-defence discipline; the name is derived from the Korean words ‘tae’, meaning kick, ‘kwon’, a punch or other blow with the hand or fist, and ‘do’, which is a way or method of operation. Among the general public, taekwondo is distinguished from other martial arts by its high speed, sweeping kicks and emphatic punches. As with judo, taekwondo was developed as a sport that is also representative of a moral code, where principles of loyalty, faithfulness, respect, and the preservation of an indomitable spirit form a significant part of taekwondo training. Beginning in 1945, shortly after the end of World War II and Japanese Occupation, new martial arts schools called kwans opened in Seoul. These schools were established by Korean martial artists with backgrounds in Japanese and Chinese martial arts. At the time, indigenous disciplines (such as Taekkyeon) were being forgotten, due to years of decline and repression by the Japanese colonial government. The umbrella term traditional Taekwondo typically refers to the martial arts practiced by the kwans during the 1940s and 1950s, though in reality the term ‘Taekwondo’ had not yet been coined at that time, and indeed each kwan (school) was practicing its own unique style of the Korean art.
Which of the following is NOT a principle of Taekwondo?
expl:
The principle that is NOT associated with Taekwondo is: Disrespect

In the passage, it is mentioned that Taekwondo is developed as a sport that is representative of a moral code. The principles of Taekwondo training include:

  1. Loyalty: This is a fundamental principle in Taekwondo, emphasizing allegiance and faithfulness to the discipline, one's instructor, and fellow practitioners.

  2. Indomitable spirit: This principle reflects the unyielding and unconquerable nature of the spirit. It encourages practitioners to be resilient, determined, and not easily subdued or defeated.

  3. Faithfulness: This refers to the quality of being loyal, steadfast, and true. It is about maintaining commitment and faith in the practice of Taekwondo.

The concept of "Disrespect" is not aligned with the principles of Taekwondo. Taekwondo emphasizes respect for oneself, instructors, fellow practitioners, and the discipline as a whole. Disrespect would go against the core values of Taekwondo, which promote positive and respectful behavior within the martial arts community.

Therefore, "Disrespect" is the principle that is NOT associated with Taekwondo.

Read the given passage and answer the question that follows.
As a result of increasing population and expansion of residential areas, forest lands are being encroached. This is not all; even the wildlife is under extreme threat. As our fauna is facing a dearth of adequate shelter in forests, they are heading towards towns and hence get killed by hunters. Consequently, many animal species have either become extinct or are on the verge of extinction. The Black Buck is almost endangered and found only in two countries, Nepal and India. In India, this antelope is found in many national parks like Guindy National Park, Point Calimere and Vellandu sanctuaries of Tamil Nadu, Rollapadu of Andra Pradesh, few parts of Rajasthan and Haryana. As far as their habitat is concerned, they live in open grasslands, dry areas or thinly populated areas and near water resources. They live in the desert areas of Rajasthan and coastal areas because they cannot sustain cold climate. They are the fastest running animals on this planet. Further, this animal is active during the day, but slows down in its activities after mid-day. They are social beings. Hence, they move with their herds, which can vary from 3 to 23 mates. They cohabit twice in a year and give birth twice in a year.
Prior to independence, this antelope was extensively hunted which affected their population so much that this species has reached the stage of extinction in many parts of the country. Poachers kill them mainly for material gain. Its skin has an enormous value in the market. In order to protect this species, the IUCN has declared this species nearly threatened. Hence, under Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act of 1972, numerous stern measures have been taken. To specify a few, Kaimur Wildlife Sanctuary (Bihar), Gir Forest National Park, Velavadar Wildlife Sanctuary (Gujarat), National Chambal Sanctuary, etc. Despite these acts, hunting is adversely affecting our wildlife. There are some solutions to this problem but the best one is to boycott the products made from endangered species at an international level. This seems to be effective but will it prevent animal hunting? That’s a question.

expl:
The author is expressing concern over the threat to wildlife, particularly the Black Buck, and the impact of hunting on endangered species. The correct answer is: Concerned

qhtml:
Read the given passage and answer the question that follows.
As a result of increasing population and expansion of residential areas, forest lands are being encroached. This is not all; even the wildlife is under extreme threat. As our fauna is facing a dearth of adequate shelter in forests, they are heading towards towns and hence get killed by hunters. Consequently, many animal species have either become extinct or are on the verge of extinction. The Black Buck is almost endangered and found only in two countries, Nepal and India. In India, this antelope is found in many national parks like Guindy National Park, Point Calimere and Vellandu sanctuaries of Tamil Nadu, Rollapadu of Andra Pradesh, few parts of Rajasthan and Haryana. As far as their habitat is concerned, they live in open grasslands, dry areas or thinly populated areas and near water resources. They live in the desert areas of Rajasthan and coastal areas because they cannot sustain cold climate. They are the fastest running animals on this planet. Further, this animal is active during the day, but slows down in its activities after mid-day. They are social beings. Hence, they move with their herds, which can vary from 3 to 23 mates. They cohabit twice in a year and give birth twice in a year.
Prior to independence, this antelope was extensively hunted which affected their population so much that this species has reached the stage of extinction in many parts of the country. Poachers kill them mainly for material gain. Its skin has an enormous value in the market. In order to protect this species, the IUCN has declared this species nearly threatened. Hence, under Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act of 1972, numerous stern measures have been taken. To specify a few, Kaimur Wildlife Sanctuary (Bihar), Gir Forest National Park, Velavadar Wildlife Sanctuary (Gujarat), National Chambal Sanctuary, etc. Despite these acts, hunting is adversely affecting our wildlife. There are some solutions to this problem but the best one is to boycott the products made from endangered species at an international level. This seems to be effective but will it prevent animal hunting? That’s a question.
What is the theme of this passage?
expl: The passage primarily discusses the threat to wildlife, particularly the Black Buck, due to habitat loss, hunting, and the effects of population growth and land encroachment. The focus is on the endangered species and the efforts to protect them, which makes "Endangered species" the most appropriate theme.
raw_sol: The passage primarily discusses the threat to wildlife, particularly the Black Buck, due to habitat loss, hunting, and the effects of population growth and land encroachment. The focus is on the endangered species and the efforts to protect them, which makes "Endangered species" the most appropriate theme.

Poachers kill them mainly for material gain. Its skin has an enormous value in the market. In order to protect this species, the IUCN has declared this species nearly threatened. Hence, under Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act of 1972, numerous stern measures have been taken. To specify a few, Kaimur Wildlife Sanctuary (Bihar), Gir Forest National Park, Velavadar Wildlife Sanctuary (Gujarat), National Chambal Sanctuary, etc. Despite these acts, hunting is adversely affecting our wildlife. There are some solutions to this problem but the best one is to boycott the products made from endangered species at an international level. This seems to be effective but will it prevent animal hunting? That’s a question.
Choose the word which closely means ‘adversely’.

Lena was an avid explorer. She had a deep fascination for the mysteries hidden within the dense forests. One day, while wandering through a secluded forest, she stumbled upon an ancient-looking map half-buried in the undergrowth. The map depicted a trail that led to a legendary waterfall rumoured to possess magical properties. Driven by her curiosity, Lena decided to follow the trail.
As she walked deeper into the forest, the atmosphere grew more enchanting. Sunlight filtered through the thick canopy, casting dappled patterns on the ground. The sound of rustling leaves and distant bird calls created a symphony of nature around her. Guided by the map's markings, Lena navigated through challenging terrains and crossed a narrow rope bridge suspended over a crystal-clear stream.
Finally, after hours of journeying, Lena arrived at the foot of the legendary waterfall. Its cascading waters sparkled like diamonds in the sunlight, and a gentle mist enveloped the surroundings. Lena felt a sense of wonder and tranquillity as she dipped her hand in the cool waters, as if the legends were coming alive. She sat by the waterfall, captivated by its beauty, pondering the ancient stories that had led her here.
What intrigued Lena's curiosity in the forest?
opts: She stumbled upon an ancient map.
She heard whispers in the wind.

Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:
The story “The Summer of the Beautiful White Horse” is a pleasant and interesting one that highlights the purity of youthfulness and the strong moral values of the Armenian Garoghlanian tribe. The story revolves around the lives of two cousins, Aram and Mourad, who belong to a poor family but are known for their honest nature. Early one morning, Aram is amazed to see his cousin Mourad riding a beautiful white horse. As the boys could not afford such a horse, Aram suspects that the horse could have been ridden without permission, but his excitement to ride the horse makes him forget his suspicion momentarily.
The two boys spend a few days secretly enjoying the rides and feel a deep connection with the animal. However, when they meet the horse’s owner, John Byro, and hear his sad story, they feel a sense of guilt. Though Byro recognizes his horse, he is too impressed by the tribe’s reputation to accuse the boys. His faith in silence is deeply touching for the boys. Finally, Mourad decides to secretly return the horse to its proper stable.
The story beautifully depicts how good values and a high moral standard can direct young hearts in the right direction.
What message does the story convey through Mourad’s decision to return the horse?
opts: Honesty and strong values guide one towards the right actions
expl:
The deciding lines.

"Finally, Mourad decides to secretly return the horse to its proper stable."

"The story beautifully depicts how good values and a high moral standard can direct young hearts in the right direction."

Join them.

Returning the horse is the right action; the last line names its source — good values and a high moral standard.

That is: honesty and strong values guide one towards the right actions (ईमानदारी और दृढ़ मूल्य सही कर्म की ओर ले जाते हैं).

Answer: Honesty and strong values guide one towards the right actions

Why the others are wrong.

• Poverty leads to irresponsible behavior = being poor makes people careless (ग़रीबी से ग़ैर-ज़िम्मेदार व्यवहार) — the boys are poor yet return the horse; the story shows the reverse.

• Adventure is more important than rules = thrill matters more than what is right (रोमांच नियमों से बड़ा) — Mourad gives up the adventure to do the right thing.

• One should never trust others blindly = be suspicious of everyone (किसी पर आँख मूँदकर भरोसा न करें) — Byro's trust is shown as touching, and it is rewarded by the horse's return.

Word help.

depicts = shows, portrays (चित्रित करता है).

The last line of a story-passage usually states its moral — read it first for theme questions.

qhtml:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:
The events in Rajamahendravaram in Andhra Pradesh involving the mass poisoning of consumers by milk contaminated with ethylene glycol sound a regulatory alarm. As of March 8, the death toll was 11, with approximately 20 other people, including infants, hospitalised. Milk is a staple in Indian households and contamination by an industrial compound already infamous in India for its lethality carries the potential to trigger a crisis of confidence in local, unbranded milk supplies. Children and the elderly are most affected by ethylene glycol poisoning due to their higher metabolic sensitivity and lower renal reserves, respectively. This could push people towards pasteurised milk from regulated cooperatives such as Amul or Vijaya, which seems desirable, but a large share of milk is also distributed in India through small vendors. Food-safety compliance is as much about punishing bad actors as about reducing the cost of doing the right thing. In the informal supply chain, cold-chain monitoring and hygiene inspections are almost entirely absent, leaving room for contamination. Subsidised testing kits and cooperative chilling facilities can thus reduce the risk at small dairies. Regulators may also consider safe-harbour provisions that ease penalties for dairy operators who report contamination at their facilities; this could also encourage early disclosure, giving authorities time to save lives.
(Source: Bitter milk: On the Rajamahendravaram milk adulteration case - The Hindu, March 10)
What is a potential consequence of the contamination mentioned in the text?
opts: A complete ban on the sale of milk in Andhra Pradesh.
A shift in consumer preference toward pasteurised milk.
An increase in the price of testing kits for small vendors.
The immediate closure of all informal milk supply chains.
expl:
The deciding lines.

"contamination … carries the potential to trigger a crisis of confidence in local, unbranded milk supplies."

"This could push people towards pasteurised milk from regulated cooperatives such as Amul or Vijaya".

Read the signal words.

potential and could mark a possible result (संभावित परिणाम).

People losing trust in loose milk and moving to packaged, pasteurised milk = a shift in consumer preference toward pasteurised milk (उपभोक्ताओं की पसंद का पाश्चुरीकृत दूध की ओर झुकाव).

Answer: A shift in consumer preference toward pasteurised milk.

Why the others are wrong.

• A complete ban on the sale of milk = stopping all milk sales (दूध की बिक्री पर पूर्ण प्रतिबंध) — no ban is mentioned; milk is called a household staple.

• An increase in the price of testing kits = kits becoming costlier (जाँच किट का महँगा होना) — the passage wants kits subsidised (अनुदानित), i.e. cheaper.

• The immediate closure of all informal milk supply chains = shutting all small vendors at once (अनौपचारिक आपूर्ति का तुरंत बंद होना) — the passage says a large share of milk still comes through small vendors and suggests making them safer, not closing them.

Word help.

staple = a basic item used every day (रोज़मर्रा की मूल वस्तु).

pasteurised = heated to kill germs (पाश्चुरीकृत, कीटाणु-रहित किया गया).

In a "consequence" question, look for could, may, potential — the passage's own forecast.

The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part which contains a grammatical error (ignore any punctuation error, if any). If there is no error in the sentence, then select 'No Error'.
The vibrant colors (a) / of the Holi festival (b) / were dispersed on the air. (c) / No error. (d)
expl:
Rule: things spread through the atmosphere are in the air (हवा में), or dispersed into the air.

on the air is an idiom meaning being broadcast on radio or TV (प्रसारित हो रहा).

Example: The smell of food hung in the air. / The programme is on the air at 9 pm.

Find the error.

Part (c) were dispersed on the air → were dispersed in (into) the air.

Corrected: The vibrant colors of the Holi festival were dispersed in the air.

Answer: (3) were dispersed on the air.

Why the others are fine.

• The vibrant colors — plural subject; vibrant = bright and lively (चटकीले).

• of the Holi festival — correct article and preposition.

• No error — wrong, since part (c) carries the preposition error.

In the air = in the atmosphere; on the air = on radio/TV.

In the given passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage intently and choose the most appropriate option to fill in each blank:
Democracies are usually credited with being resilient, yet the past indicates that they can be quite vulnerable. Those institutions that are meant to protect freedom can weaken when citizens become disconnected or when politicians take advantage of (1) ______ within the system. Gradual removal of checks and balances might not raise an alarm until it is too late.
One of the central factors is the state of public discourse. When argument gets polarised and facts are sacrificed to (2) ______, democratic conventions start to disintegrate. The media is responsible here, either as a watchdog or as a megaphone for disinformation. The advent of echo chambers has made it simpler for individuals to shun (3) ______ perspectives, strengthening tribalism.
Economic inequality is another threat. When significant portions of the populace feel left out of prosperity, they can lose confidence in democratic processes and seek (4) ______ alternatives. This cynicism can be taken advantage of by populist movements that make quick fixes but destroy democratic ideas.
Democracy must be safeguarded with vigilance, participation, and a willingness to search for truth. Without these, even the most entrenched systems can become (5) ______, susceptible to rot from within.
What should come in the place of blank number 5?
expl:
The deciding words.

"Without these, even the most entrenched systems can become (5) [blank], susceptible to rot from within."

What the blank needs.

even the most entrenched signals a contrast — strong systems turning weak.

The phrase after the comma, susceptible to rot, restates the blank.

vulnerable = open to attack or harm (असुरक्षित, भेद्य) — and it echoes the opening line: "they can be quite vulnerable".

Answer: (2) Vulnerable

Why the others are wrong.

• strong = powerful, firm (मज़बूत) — the opposite of what "even the most entrenched" sets up.

• honest = truthful (ईमानदार) — describes people, not a system decaying from within.

• sincere = genuine, without pretence (निष्कपट) — also a personal quality with no link to "rot".

Word help.

entrenched = firmly established, hard to remove (सुदृढ़ रूप से जमा हुआ).

susceptible = easily affected or harmed (संवेदनशील, प्रभावित होने योग्य).

"Even the most …" sets up a fall: entrenched yet vulnerable.

Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:
The story “The Summer of the Beautiful White Horse” is a pleasant and interesting one that highlights the purity of youthfulness and the strong moral values of the Armenian Garoghlanian tribe. The story revolves around the lives of two cousins, Aram and Mourad, who belong to a poor family but are known for their honest nature. Early one morning, Aram is amazed to see his cousin Mourad riding a beautiful white horse. As the boys could not afford such a horse, Aram suspects that the horse could have been ridden without permission, but his excitement to ride the horse makes him forget his suspicion momentarily.
The two boys spend a few days secretly enjoying the rides and feel a deep connection with the animal. However, when they meet the horse’s owner, John Byro, and hear his sad story, they feel a sense of guilt. Though Byro recognizes his horse, he is too impressed by the tribe’s reputation to accuse the boys. His faith in silence is deeply touching for the boys. Finally, Mourad decides to secretly return the horse to its proper stable.
The story beautifully depicts how good values and a high moral standard can direct young hearts in the right direction.
Why was Aram surprised when he first saw Mourad in the morning?
opts: Because Mourad was riding a beautiful white horse
Because Mourad had bought a new bicycle
Because Mourad was moving to another town

qhtml:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
The guests are being served dinner by the chef.
opts: The chef has served dinner to the guests.
The chef serves dinner to the guests.
The chef is serving dinner to the guests.
The chef will serve dinner to the guests.
expl:
Rule: is/am/are + being + V3 is the present continuous passive (अपूर्ण वर्तमान कर्मवाच्य).

Its active form is subject + is/am/are + V-ing + object.

Example: The car is being washed by Ravi. → Ravi is washing the car.

Apply it.

Agent the chef → subject.

are being served → is serving (singular chef).

The chef is serving dinner to the guests.

Answer: (3) The chef is serving dinner to the guests.

Why the others are wrong.

• has served — present perfect active (पूर्ण वर्तमान); the action is still going on, not completed.

• serves — simple present active (सामान्य वर्तमान); it loses the being (continuous) sense.

• will serve — simple future active (सामान्य भविष्य); the passive is in the present.

"being + V3" in passive ⇔ "-ing" in active.

What should come in the place of blank number 1?
expl:
The deciding words.

"politicians take advantage of (1) [blank] within the system. Gradual removal of checks and balances …"

What the blank needs.

A plural noun for something politicians can exploit inside the system — a weakness or opening.

gaps = openings, loopholes (खामियाँ, रिक्तियाँ) — exactly what one "takes advantage of".

Answer: (3) Gaps

Why the others are wrong.

• strength = power, firmness (शक्ति) — the paragraph is about how institutions weaken; exploiting strength makes no sense, and it is singular.

• balances = counterweights (संतुलन) — the next line speaks of removing checks and balances, so they are what is lost, not what is exploited.

• faults = defects, mistakes (दोष) — close, but faults suggests blame or errors; the passage means loopholes, openings that can be used.

Word help.

resilient = able to recover quickly from difficulty (लचीला, शीघ्र उबरने वाला).

checks and balances = the limits each branch of government places on the others (नियंत्रण और संतुलन).

You take advantage of gaps (loopholes) in a system, not of its faults.

expl:
Meaning: Renaissance = rebirth, revival; especially the revival of art and learning in 14th–16th century Europe (पुनर्जागरण).

Build the spelling.

Re + nais + sance — French renaître, "to be born again".

One n after Re, then -ai-, then double ss, ending -ance.

Answer: (1) Renaissance

Why the others are wrong.

• Rinassance — Ri instead of Re, and -ai- collapsed to -a-.

• Rennesance — double nn and a single s; both are reversed from -naiss-.

• Ranessance — Ra instead of Re, and the i of -ai- is missing.

Re-NAIS-sance: one n, then "ai", then double s — the word is "re + naissance (birth)".

qhtml:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:
The events in Rajamahendravaram in Andhra Pradesh involving the mass poisoning of consumers by milk contaminated with ethylene glycol sound a regulatory alarm. As of March 8, the death toll was 11, with approximately 20 other people, including infants, hospitalised. Milk is a staple in Indian households and contamination by an industrial compound already infamous in India for its lethality carries the potential to trigger a crisis of confidence in local, unbranded milk supplies. Children and the elderly are most affected by ethylene glycol poisoning due to their higher metabolic sensitivity and lower renal reserves, respectively. This could push people towards pasteurised milk from regulated cooperatives such as Amul or Vijaya, which seems desirable, but a large share of milk is also distributed in India through small vendors. Food-safety compliance is as much about punishing bad actors as about reducing the cost of doing the right thing. In the informal supply chain, cold-chain monitoring and hygiene inspections are almost entirely absent, leaving room for contamination. Subsidised testing kits and cooperative chilling facilities can thus reduce the risk at small dairies. Regulators may also consider safe-harbour provisions that ease penalties for dairy operators who report contamination at their facilities; this could also encourage early disclosure, giving authorities time to save lives.
(Source: Bitter milk: On the Rajamahendravaram milk adulteration case - The Hindu, March 10)
Which measure does the author suggest to improve small dairy safety?
opts: Make penalties tougher for all dairy owners.
Require all milk to be sold through Amul or Vijaya only.
Providing subsidised testing kits and cooperative chilling facilities.
Use machines to check cold storage instead of people.
expl:
The deciding line.

"Subsidised testing kits and cooperative chilling facilities can thus reduce the risk at small dairies."

Match it.

The question's words small dairy safety mirror the passage's reduce the risk at small dairies.

Option (c) repeats the measure word for word: cheaper testing kits (अनुदानित जाँच किट) and shared chilling plants (सहकारी शीतलन सुविधाएँ).

Answer: Providing subsidised testing kits and cooperative chilling facilities.

Why the others are wrong.

• Make penalties tougher = harsher punishment (कड़े दंड) — the author goes the other way, suggesting safe-harbour provisions that ease penalties for those who report.

• Require all milk to be sold through Amul or Vijaya only = a monopoly for cooperatives (केवल अमूल या विजया से बिक्री) — the passage accepts that small vendors supply a large share and wants them made safe.

• Use machines … instead of people = replacing human inspectors (मनुष्यों की जगह मशीनें) — the passage only says cold-chain monitoring is absent; it never proposes machines.

Word help.

subsidised = partly paid for by the government, so cheaper (सरकारी सहायता से सस्ता).

cold-chain = keeping a product cold all the way from producer to buyer (शीत शृंखला).

When the question echoes a phrase from the passage, the answer sits in that very sentence.

disclosure = making something known (प्रकटीकरण, खुलासा).

A safe harbour rewards the one who tells — early reporting in exchange for lighter punishment.

Change the following sentence into the Active form.
He was seen to have been struggling with the technical presentation for over an hour by the project manager.
opts: The project manager saw him struggling with the technical presentation for over an hour.
He struggled with the technical presentation for over an hour, and the project manager saw him.
The project manager saw that he was struggling with the technical presentation for over an hour.
The project manager had seen him struggling with the technical presentation for over an hour.
expl:
Rule: verbs of perception (see, hear, watch) in the passive take a to-infinitive (was seen to …); in the active the to drops and the object takes a bare infinitive or -ing form.

was seen is simple past passive (सामान्य भूत कर्मवाच्य) → active saw + object + V-ing.

Example: She was heard to sing. → They heard her sing / singing.

Apply it.

Agent the project manager → subject.

was seen → saw; he → object him.

to have been struggling (an action in progress) → struggling.

The project manager saw him struggling with the technical presentation for over an hour.

Answer: (1) The project manager saw him struggling with the technical presentation for over an hour.

Why the others are wrong.

• He struggled …, and the project manager saw him. — a compound sentence that only paraphrases; it is not the active voice of the given sentence (वाच्य परिवर्तन नहीं, केवल भावार्थ).

• saw that he was struggling — a that-clause reports a conclusion (mental seeing); the passive was seen to converts to object + -ing, not to a noun clause.

• had seen — past perfect (पूर्ण भूत); the passive was seen is simple past, so the active is saw.

Passive "was seen to …" ⇔ active "saw him …ing" — drop the "to".

Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:
Mr. Dash said, "What a costly thing gold has become!"
opts: Mr. Dash lamented that gold has become a very costly thing.
Mr. Dash shouted that gold did become a very costly thing.
Mr. Dash exclaimed that gold had been becoming a very costly thing.
Mr. Dash exclaimed that gold had become a very costly thing.
expl:
Rule: exclamatory sentence → indirect speech (विस्मयादिबोधक वाक्य का अप्रत्यक्ष कथन):

• said → exclaimed (with joy / sorrow / surprise as the tone fits)

• What a / How → very (or great), placed before the adjective; statement order; full stop

• joiner that; past reporting verb → present perfect has become → had become

Example: She said, "How beautiful the rose is!" → She exclaimed that the rose was very beautiful.

Apply it.

said → exclaimed

What a costly thing → a very costly thing

has become → had become

Answer: (4) Mr. Dash exclaimed that gold had become a very costly thing.

Why the others are wrong.

• lamented … has become — lamented (शोक प्रकट किया) is possible in tone, but has become is not shifted back to had become.

• shouted … did become — shouted (चिल्लाया) is not the reporting verb for an exclamation, and did become is emphatic simple past, not the past perfect.

• had been becoming — past perfect continuous (पूर्ण अपूर्ण भूत); has become (present perfect) goes only to had become.

What a / How → very; has → had.

• delirium = a confused, disturbed state of mind, often from illness (सन्निपात, प्रलाप) — the opposite of pleasant.

qhtml:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'
The project was completed before less than three months.
expl:
Rule: to say how long something took, use in + a period of time (अवधि के भीतर — in).

Example: She learnt to swim in two weeks.

before needs a point of time (before Monday), never "before less than three months".

Apply it.

less than three months is a duration, so: The project was completed in less than three months.

Answer: (3) completed in

Why the others are wrong.

• completed on — on is for days and dates (on Monday, on 5 May) (दिन/तिथि के लिए), not a length of time.

• completed at — at is for a clock time or a point (at noon, at 5 pm) (समय-बिंदु के लिए).

• No substitution — before less than three months is ungrammatical, so a change is needed.

Finished IN a period, ON a date, AT a time, BEFORE a deadline.

qhtml:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:
The events in Rajamahendravaram in Andhra Pradesh involving the mass poisoning of consumers by milk contaminated with ethylene glycol sound a regulatory alarm. As of March 8, the death toll was 11, with approximately 20 other people, including infants, hospitalised. Milk is a staple in Indian households and contamination by an industrial compound already infamous in India for its lethality carries the potential to trigger a crisis of confidence in local, unbranded milk supplies. Children and the elderly are most affected by ethylene glycol poisoning due to their higher metabolic sensitivity and lower renal reserves, respectively. This could push people towards pasteurised milk from regulated cooperatives such as Amul or Vijaya, which seems desirable, but a large share of milk is also distributed in India through small vendors. Food-safety compliance is as much about punishing bad actors as about reducing the cost of doing the right thing. In the informal supply chain, cold-chain monitoring and hygiene inspections are almost entirely absent, leaving room for contamination. Subsidised testing kits and cooperative chilling facilities can thus reduce the risk at small dairies. Regulators may also consider safe-harbour provisions that ease penalties for dairy operators who report contamination at their facilities; this could also encourage early disclosure, giving authorities time to save lives.
(Source: Bitter milk: On the Rajamahendravaram milk adulteration case - The Hindu, March 10)
According to the passage, why are the elderly specifically more vulnerable to ethylene glycol poisoning?
opts: Because they consume more unbranded milk than infants.
Because they lack access to regulated cooperatives.
expl:
The deciding line.

"Children and the elderly are most affected by ethylene glycol poisoning due to their higher metabolic sensitivity and lower renal reserves, respectively."

Read "respectively".

Respectively (क्रमशः) pairs the two lists in the same order.

1st with 1st: children → higher metabolic sensitivity

2nd with 2nd: elderly → lower renal reserves

So the elderly suffer because of lower renal reserves = weaker kidney capacity (गुर्दों की कम आरक्षित क्षमता).

Answer: Due to their lower renal reserves.

Why the others are wrong.

• higher metabolic sensitivity = the body reacting more strongly to a substance (अधिक चयापचय संवेदनशीलता) — by "respectively" this belongs to children, not the elderly.

• consume more unbranded milk than infants = drinking more loose, local milk (शिशुओं से अधिक खुला दूध पीना) — the passage never compares how much milk any group drinks.

• lack access to regulated cooperatives = cannot reach Amul or Vijaya milk (नियंत्रित सहकारी दूध तक पहुँच न होना) — cooperatives are mentioned as a remedy, not as a reason for the elderly's risk.

Word help.

renal = of the kidneys (गुर्दे से संबंधित).

ethylene glycol = a toxic industrial liquid used in antifreeze and coolants (एथिलीन ग्लाइकॉल, एक विषैला औद्योगिक रसायन).

"Respectively" is a matching instruction — pair the lists in order, never swap them.

qhtml: Which of the following options is NOT one of the meanings of the homonym 'suspension'?
opts: The act of temporarily stopping or halting something
A mixture in which particles are dispersed in a fluid but not dissolved
A state of uncertainty or excitement about what will happen next
A type of mechanical system used in vehicles to absorb shocks
expl:
Meaning: suspension = the act of hanging or holding something up, and from that several meanings (निलंबन / निलंबन तंत्र / निलंबित मिश्रण).

The real meanings.

• a temporary stop — suspension of play, suspension from duty (निलंबन, अस्थायी रोक)

• in chemistry, a mixture with undissolved particles — chalk in water (निलंबन/निलंबित विलयन)

• in vehicles, the shock-absorbing system (सस्पेंशन, झटके सहने का तंत्र)

The odd one.

"A state of uncertainty or excitement about what will happen next" is the meaning of suspense (उत्सुकता, रोमांच), not suspension.

Answer: (3) A state of uncertainty or excitement about what will happen next

Why the others are fine.

• temporarily stopping — a true meaning: the suspension of train services.

• particles dispersed but not dissolved — a true meaning in chemistry.

• mechanical system to absorb shocks — a true meaning: a car's suspension.

A thriller keeps you in SUSPENSE; a car rides on its SUSPENSION.

qhtml:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
P: In contrast, applying a heavy moisturizer first would block the absorption of lighter serums.
Q: Hence, layering products from thinnest to thickest consistency ensures maximum efficacy for every ingredient.
R: Typically, a balanced skincare routine begins with a gentle cleanser to remove daily impurities.
S: Additionally, active treatments like vitamin C should be applied directly onto clean, damp skin.
expl:
Opener test.

R — Typically, a balanced skincare routine begins with … — sets up the topic and the first step: the opener.

S (Additionally), P (In contrast) and Q (Hence) each need an earlier sentence.

Only option (d) begins with R.

Links.

R → S: Additionally gives the next step — actives go onto clean, damp skin, i.e. skin just washed by R's cleanser.

S → P: In contrast shows the wrong way — a heavy moisturizer first would block lighter serums.

P → Q: Hence concludes the rule — layer from thinnest to thickest.

The paragraph.

Typically, a balanced skincare routine begins with a gentle cleanser to remove daily impurities. Additionally, active treatments like vitamin C should be applied directly onto clean, damp skin. In contrast, applying a heavy moisturizer first would block the absorption of lighter serums. Hence, layering products from thinnest to thickest consistency ensures maximum efficacy for every ingredient.

Answer: RSPQ

Word help.

efficacy = the power to produce the intended result (प्रभावकारिता).

absorption = soaking in (अवशोषण).

"Hence" closes — it states the rule the earlier sentences have built up.

qhtml:
In the given passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage intently and choose the most appropriate option to fill in each blank:
Democracies are usually credited with being resilient, yet the past indicates that they can be quite vulnerable. Those institutions that are meant to protect freedom can weaken when citizens become disconnected or when politicians take advantage of (1) ______ within the system. Gradual removal of checks and balances might not raise an alarm until it is too late.
One of the central factors is the state of public discourse. When argument gets polarised and facts are sacrificed to (2) ______, democratic conventions start to disintegrate. The media is responsible here, either as a watchdog or as a megaphone for disinformation. The advent of echo chambers has made it simpler for individuals to shun (3) ______ perspectives, strengthening tribalism.
Economic inequality is another threat. When significant portions of the populace feel left out of prosperity, they can lose confidence in democratic processes and seek (4) ______ alternatives. This cynicism can be taken advantage of by populist movements that make quick fixes but destroy democratic ideas.
Democracy must be safeguarded with vigilance, participation, and a willingness to search for truth. Without these, even the most entrenched systems can become (5) ______, susceptible to rot from within.
What should come in the place of blank number 2?
expl:
The deciding words.

"When argument gets polarised and facts are sacrificed to (2) [blank], democratic conventions start to disintegrate."

What the blank needs.

Something in public discourse that replaces facts in an argument.

rhetoric = persuasive or showy speech that may lack substance (लच्छेदार/भड़काऊ भाषणबाज़ी).

The phrase "facts sacrificed to rhetoric" is the standard collocation for debate that runs on slogans instead of evidence.

Answer: (4) Rhetoric

Why the others are wrong.

• lies = deliberate falsehoods (झूठ) — too blunt; the next line separately mentions disinformation, and the blank is about the style of argument.

• emotions = feelings (भावनाएँ) — possible in ordinary speech, but the paragraph is about discourse and argument, which points to speech-making, not feelings.

• biases = prejudices (पूर्वाग्रह) — biases distort judgement, but facts are not "sacrificed to" a bias in a debate.

Word help.

discourse = public discussion and debate (विमर्श).

polarised = split into two sharply opposed camps (ध्रुवीकृत).

Discourse + argument + polarised = rhetoric: facts lose to fine-sounding words.

qhtml:
Choose the most suitable preposition from the given options to fill in the blank in the following sentence:
The decision was consistent ______ company policy.
expl:
Rule: the adjective consistent takes with when it means "in agreement with" (के अनुरूप).

Example: His words are not consistent with his actions.

Apply it.

The decision was consistent with company policy. — it agreed with the policy.

Answer: (1) with

Why the others are wrong.

• to — goes with according to, similar to, contrary to (के अनुसार/विपरीत), never with consistent.

• by — marks the agent or means (के द्वारा); "consistent by" is not an English collocation.

• for — shows purpose or benefit (के लिए); it cannot express agreement.

Consistent WITH, in line WITH, in keeping WITH — agreement takes "with".
